artigo.texto: Mercado global de cartuchos de armazenamento de hidreto metálico: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do Mercado de Cartuchos de Armazenamento de Hidreto Metálico até 2035: Demanda por Resiliência de Data Centers Impulsiona CAGR de 12%-16% Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de cartuchos de armazenamento de hidreto metálico, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de cartuchos de armazenamento de hidreto metálico entra em uma fase de expansão acelerada, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa composta anual de 12% a 16% entre 2026 e 2035. Esses dispositivos de armazenamento de hidrogênio em estado sólido, que absorvem e liberam hidrogênio por meio de ligas de hidreto metálico, vêm ganhando tração como alternativa mais segura e de baixa pressão aos cilindros de gás comprimido em aplicações estacionárias e móveis. A expansão do mercado é sustentada pela ampliação dos sistemas estacionários de backup com células a combustível, pela necessidade de armazenamento seguro de hidrogênio em projetos de integração de renováveis e pela emergência da resiliência de data centers como vetor crítico de demanda. Em 2026, as aplicações de infraestrutura de rede e de backup industrial respondem juntas por cerca de 60% a 65% do volume global de cartuchos, mas espera-se que projetos de data centers e de escala utilitária dobrem sua participação até 2030. A oferta permanece concentrada em menos de uma dúzia de fabricantes especializados no mundo, e as restrições de capacidade na etapa de processamento de ligas estão alongando os prazos de entrega para 14 a 20 semanas no caso dos cartuchos de grau premium, o que cria pressão de alta sobre os preços no curto prazo. À medida que o mercado amadurece, os clientes passam a dar mais peso à vida útil em ciclos e à densidade gravimétrica, e as especificações premium que superam 1.500 ciclos completos de carga e descarga conquistam uma fatia crescente das vendas unitárias. Pressões regulatórias para reduzir a intensidade de carbono na energia de backup, sobretudo na Europa e em parte da Ásia, também estão acelerando a qualificação dos cartuchos de hidreto metálico como solução preferencial de armazenamento de hidrogênio para infraestruturas críticas. O cenário-base para o mercado global de cartuchos de armazenamento de hidreto metálico projeta crescimento robusto até 2035, com taxa composta anual de 12% a 16% entre 2026 e 2035. Essa projeção pressupõe apoio contínuo de políticas públicas à infraestrutura de hidrogênio, reduções constantes de custo na produção de ligas de hidreto metálico e adoção acelerada de sistemas de backup com células a combustível em data centers e na infraestrutura de rede. O índice de mercado, fixado em 100 em 2025, deve alcançar 350 até 2035, o que reflete um aumento de mais de três vezes em termos reais. O crescimento será concentrado no curto prazo, à medida que operadores de data centers e concessionárias de energia busquem substituir geradores a diesel e bancos de baterias de chumbo-ácido por armazenamento de hidrogênio mais limpo e de maior duração. Até 2030, a resiliência de data centers deve dobrar sua participação na demanda por cartuchos e se tornar o segmento de uso final de crescimento mais rápido. Restrições do lado da oferta, especialmente no processamento de ligas de terras raras, devem persistir até o fim da década de 2020, mantendo prazos de entrega elevados e sustentando preços premium para cartuchos de longa vida útil em ciclos. Com a entrada em operação de nova capacidade de processamento de ligas na Ásia-Pacífico e na América do Norte após 2028, as condições de oferta devem se aliviar, permitindo adoção mais ampla em aplicações industriais e de integração de renováveis. O cenário-base não pressupõe reduções revolucionárias de custo a partir de químicas alternativas, mas sim melhorias incrementais na formulação de ligas e na automação da manufatura, que reduzem os custos dos cartuchos em 15% a 20% até 2035. Entre os riscos de baixa estão a expansão da infraestrutura de hidrogênio mais lenta do que o esperado e a concorrência do armazenamento em baterias de íons de lítio, enquanto o potencial de alta existe caso a precificação de carbono acelere a aposentadoria dos sistemas de backup movidos a combustíveis fósseis. artigo.texto: Blaine County leaders on Tuesday are scheduled to consider approving an ordinance to establish a temporary emergency moratorium on the issuance of development permits for data centers. The proposed ordinance—put forth by Commissioner Lindsay Mollineaux—would disallow county officials from the “receipt, processing and approval of applications” of permits for the construction of data centers in Blaine County for 182 days. The emergency moratorium also mandates that county officials in that six-month period develop a plan for a “permanent solution” to a list of “problems” associated with data centers, including the developments’ typically industrial-scale consumption of water and energy. The proposed moratorium was placed on the Tuesday agenda of the Board of County Commissioners just two days after the commissioners asked the county’s land use director, Rachel Martin, to initiate the process of drafting amendments to the zoning code to define any allowances for data centers on industrial-zoned lands. “Internally, we have been discussing for quite a while data centers and their effects on neighboring properties and the community as a whole,” Martin said to the board. “Many local jurisdictions in Idaho have started adopting codes to regulate data centers and their use.” Martin said the Land Use and Building Services Department has determined that the often-controversial developments could potentially be allowed in the county’s light-industrial zones, but only with “carefully considered” regulations and “specific parameters.” In an interview Monday, Mollineaux said she determined that the county needs to implement the emergency moratorium to allow time to analyze the complicated issue and implement appropriate regulations before any applications are made. No applications for data centers have yet been submitted to the county, Martin said last week. However, Mollineaux said, in the absence of a moratorium, any incoming applications would have to be processed under the existing zoning regulations, which don’t adequately address data centers. Data centers are buildings—sometimes extremely large—that store, process and distribute digital data and information through a vast network of electronic equipment. The rapid growth of the use of artificial intelligence—which relies heavily on data centers—in different applications has fueled a high demand for the developments and a subsequent boom in their construction. However, as more data centers are constructed, evidence of some significant negative impacts has surfaced. Detractors of AI data centers across the nation have cited water usage, energy requirements, environmental pollution and provision of a relative lack of long-term jobs as significant negative factors. Meanwhile, promoters say the developments provide thousands of well-paying jobs, fuel economic expansion, boost communities’ tax bases and help meet the needs of modern technology. The three-page proposed Blaine County moratorium cites an array of potential negative impacts, especially massive water consumption in a region stricken by drought and under strict state management of existing water resources. It states that: - “A medium-sized data center can consume up to 300,000 gallons of water per day for cooling, roughly the daily use of 1,000 households,” and that large centers can consume up to 5 million gallons per day. - “Most large data centers use evaporative cooling, which consumes water and removes it from the local watershed rather than returning it.” - Major water draws for data centers “can reduce streamflow during drought, harm aquatic habitat, and increase competition with agricultural and municipal water users.” The proposed ordinance also states that data centers: - Use a variety of dangerous chemicals and consume up to 100 megawatts of electricity, enough to power tens of thousands of homes. - “Are often at least 1,000,000 square feet in size, or approximately the size of 17 football fields,” and newer proposals are calling for even bigger facilities. The proposed moratorium concludes that the impacts of an improperly regulated data center “constitute an imminent peril to the public health, safety, and welfare of the citizens of Blaine County.” Blaine County currently has only three areas zoned for light-industrial uses, Martin said. They include: a small area south of Ketchum along state Highway 75, around Clear Creek Drive just north of The Meadows; a small area just north of Hailey along Highway 75, around Bartholomew Road; and a larger area around Glendale Road southwest of Bellevue. In crafting regulations for data centers to be added to the zoning code, the county will have to consider matters such as establishing a clear definition of data centers, what size might be permitted and what limitations might be placed on water and energy consumption, Martin told commissioners last week. The process—which will require extensive research by staff, reviews by the county’s Planning and Zoning Commission and final approval of the Board of Commissioners—should include “quite a bit of public input,” Martin said. Mollineaux said Monday that data centers have “been on everyone’s mind for a while” but she learned of the “imminent” nature of the issue at a recent Idaho Association of Counties meeting. Other counties have already taken action to regulate data centers, she said, and details of other developments in Idaho that are moving forward have come forth. Idaho is now in the “bullseye” for data centers, she said, and Blaine County needs to establish proper control. Even though industrial-zoned land in Blaine County is limited, land can be rezoned and developers can seek loopholes in existing regulations, she said. As for whether developers might propose to build a data center in one of the cities in the county, Hailey City Administrator Lisa Horowitz said she and Hailey leaders are not planning for that scenario. artigo.texto: OS DATA CENTERS CRESCEM DE IMPORTÂNCIA E JÁ SERÃO TEMA DE UM DEBATE INTERNACIONAL QUE COMEÇA AMANHÃ EM SÃO PAULO A primeira edição do Data Center World Brasil começa amanhã (6), no São Paulo Expo, em um momento em que decisões sobre energia, tributação, conectividade e capacidade computacional ganham peso na definição de onde e como serão instalados os próximos grandes projetos de data centers no país. A programação reúne debates sobre condições regulatórias, investimentos, disponibilidade de energia, conectividade, refrigeração, operação e capacidade computacional, diante de uma nova geração de aplicações de inteligência artificial que exige infraestruturas mais robustas e eficientes. Um dos temas que chegam ao congresso é o Redata, novo regime especial de tributação para serviços de data center, criado para estimular investimentos no setor. A medida será discutida às 10h30, na Opening Arena, durante o painel “Infraestrutura digital como ativo geopolítico: competitividade, investimentos, regulação e o que precisa mudar”. A conversa aborda os efeitos do programa sobre a atração de investimentos, a competitividade do país e as decisões que podem influenciar a infraestrutura digital nos próximos cinco a dez anos. O debate passa ainda pelo impacto do Confaz e do ICMS sobre a competitividade do setor. A energia é outro fator decisivo nessa equação. O avanço da inteligência artificial elevou a demanda por capacidade computacional e trouxe novos desafios para a implantação e a operação dos data centers. Localização, disponibilidade energética, eficiência e continuidade operacional estão entre os temas que atravessam a programação do congresso Na sequência, às 11h30, a roundtable “Energia como gargalo estrutural: disponibilidade, intermitência e viabilidade real” discute a oferta efetiva de energia, modelos de geração, armazenamento e alternativas para garantir estabilidade às operações. Às 14h, o painel “Como grandes empresas escolhem data centers na prática: decisões reais de custo, risco e performance” traz a perspectiva de quem utiliza essa infraestrutura e precisa equilibrar localização, latência, custo, segurança e continuidade dos serviços. A discussão sobre investimentos volta às 16h, com a roundtable “Financiamento, viabilidade e expansão: por que projetos travam — e como viabilizar na prática”, que reúne representantes do Ministério das Comunicações, BNDES, Brasscom e Patria Investments. O debate aborda capital, crédito e as condições necessárias para tirar grandes projetos do papel. A conectividade também ganha espaço entre os assuntos que ajudam a explicar a expansão do setor. O avanço das redes de alta capacidade reforça a importância de conexões estratégicas para sustentar data centers, serviços de cloud e aplicações digitais cada vez mais intensivas em processamento. No dia 7, quarta-feira, o painel “Latência, rotas globais e edge: onde a infraestrutura decide o jogo”, às 10h30, aborda a relação entre localização, conectividade e desempenho. Às 15h15, o painel “Desafios dos Hyperscalers: como planejar capacidade em um mercado imprevisível” coloca no centro da conversa o desafio de ampliar a capacidade diante do crescimento da demanda impulsionada pela IA. Logo depois, às 16h, o estudo de caso “Continuidade operacional em data centers: como se preparar para falhas, crises e eventos extremos” contempla estratégias de preparação para situações capazes de afetar as operações. Para fechar o segundo dia, às 16h30, o LATAM Leaders Panel “Data centers na América Latina: investimento, expansão e decisões de arquitetura” amplia a discussão para os movimentos de investimento e crescimento do mercado regional. A inteligência artificial ganha ainda mais espaço no último dia do congresso. Na quinta-feira, 8 de outubro, às 10h30, o C-Level Panel “Expansão na era da IA: decisões que definem bilhões em investimento” discute escolhas de infraestrutura, energia e capacidade diante da nova escala de demanda. Às 14h, o painel “Data centers AI-ready: densidade, energia e novos requisitos de infraestrutura” mostra como cargas computacionais mais intensivas estão mudando a arquitetura dos empreendimentos. O aumento da densidade dos racks pressiona sistemas elétricos e térmicos e acelera a adoção de tecnologias de refrigeração mais eficientes, como o liquid cooling. Para Leonardo Benedicto, diretor do Data Center World Brasil, a transformação provocada pela IA exige que o setor olhe para os data centers de forma mais ampla. “A inteligência artificial está mudando rapidamente a forma como pensamos os data centers. Não é apenas uma questão de aumentar capacidade. É preciso considerar energia, refrigeração, espaço e a possibilidade de ampliar as instalações ao longo do tempo. O desafio é construir uma infraestrutura que acompanhe a velocidade dessa transformação e esteja preparada para as demandas que ainda estão por vir.” A expansão do setor também tem reflexos sobre a economia. Estudo da FGV aponta que 100 MW de capacidade instalada em data centers podem representar cerca de 12,5 mil empregos, evidenciando o alcance dos investimentos em infraestrutura digital para além do mercado de tecnologia.

artigo.texto: Calgon Carbon Corporation A Kuraray company, global leader in specialty carbons. According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Impregnated Activated Carbon market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global impregnated activated carbon market is entering a phase of sustained expansion, with demand projected to grow at a compound annual rate of 5–7% between 2026 and 2035. This specialized segment of the activated carbon industry is distinguished by chemically treated carbons that selectively remove specific contaminants—such as mercury, hydrogen sulfide, ammonia, and volatile organic compounds—from gas and liquid streams. Unlike commodity activated carbon, impregnated grades command significant price premiums, often 100–200% above standard products, reflecting their engineered performance and the critical nature of their applications. The market is being reshaped by tightening environmental regulations, particularly in North America and Europe, where mercury emission limits for coal-fired power plants and industrial boilers are driving adoption. Simultaneously, the rapid expansion of biogas and renewable natural gas projects is creating new demand for impregnated carbons used in desulfurization. Food and feed processing industries are also increasingly specifying these carbons to meet stringent safety and quality standards. Supply remains concentrated among a dozen global producers, with most national markets dependent on imports. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of the market size, segmentation, competitive landscape, and regional dynamics, offering a data-driven outlook to 2035. The baseline scenario for the impregnated activated carbon market anticipates a 5–7% CAGR from 2026 to 2035, with the market index reaching approximately 180 (2025=100) by the end of the forecast period. This growth is underpinned by regulatory mandates rather than discretionary spending, providing a high degree of demand visibility. In North America and Europe, mercury and air toxics standards (MATS) and the Industrial Emissions Directive (IED) are compelling utilities and industrial operators to install or upgrade injection and fixed-bed systems using brominated or sulfur-impregnated carbons. In Asia-Pacific, while regulations are less uniform, China's ultra-low emission standards for coal-fired power and India's tightening environmental norms are creating substantial incremental demand. The biogas sector, supported by renewable energy incentives in Europe and North America, represents the fastest-growing application, with desulfurization requirements driving double-digit growth in that niche. Food and feed processing applications are also expanding, as clean-label trends and food safety regulations push processors to adopt impregnated carbons for purification. On the supply side, capacity expansions are underway in China and Southeast Asia, but qualification cycles for regulated applications remain lengthy, limiting supply elasticity. Raw material price volatility—particularly for coal-based and coconut shell precursors—poses a risk to margins, though producers have demonstrated some ability to pass through costs. Overall, the market is expected to remain tight for high-purity, certified grades, with contract-based procurement becoming the norm. The air and gas purification segment is the largest end-use sector for impregnated activated carbon, accounting for an estimated 35% of global demand. This segment is primarily driven by the need to remove mercury, dioxins, and acid gases from flue gas streams in coal-fired power plants, waste incinerators, and industrial boilers. In North America and Europe, regulations such as the Mercury and Air Toxics Standards (MATS) and the Industrial Emissions Directive (IED) mandate strict emission limits, compelling operators to adopt brominated or sulfur-impregnated carbons for mercury capture. Through 2035, demand in this segment is expected to grow at a moderate pace in developed markets as retrofits are completed, but accelerate in Asia-Pacific where China and India are tightening emission standards. Key demand-side indicators include coal-fired power generation capacity, waste incineration rates, and regulatory enforcement timelines. The segment is also seeing innovation in multi-pollutant control, where impregnated carbons are formulated to simultaneously capture mercury, SO2, and NOx, offering cost advantages. However, the long-term outlook is tempered by the gradual retirement of coal plants in some regions, offset by growth in waste-to-energy and industrial processes. Current trend: Growing due to mercury and air toxics regulations. Major trends: Increasing adoption of brominated activated carbon for mercury removal in coal-fired power plants, Development of multi-functional carbons for simultaneous removal of multiple pollutants, Growth in waste-to-energy capacity driving demand for dioxin removal, and Retrofitting of older industrial boilers with activated carbon injection systems. Representative participants: Cabot Corporation, Calgon Carbon Corporation, Jacobi Carbons, Haycarb PLC, and Donau Carbon GmbH. Water treatment represents approximately 25% of global impregnated activated carbon demand, encompassing municipal drinking water, industrial process water, and wastewater treatment. Impregnated carbons are used to remove specific contaminants such as hydrogen sulfide, chlorine, chloramines, and heavy metals like arsenic and lead. In municipal drinking water, regulations such as the U.S. Safe Drinking Water Act and the EU Drinking Water Directive are driving adoption, particularly for the removal of emerging contaminants like PFAS and pesticides. Industrial water treatment, especially in the food and beverage, pharmaceutical, and electronics sectors, requires high-purity impregnated carbons for process water purification. Thr

artigo.texto: • 13 min de lectura Até 30 de setembro de 2026, as empresas de transporte marítimo devem entregar as Licenças de Emissão da UE (EUAs) que cubram 70% das suas emissões verificadas e abrangidas a partir de 2025. A nossa equipa de Mercados de Carbono está aqui para o ajudar a compreender a sua posição e a preparar-se para o prazo, quer já tenha negociado EUAs connosco, seja um cliente nosso de energia marítima, esteja a comprar EUAs pela primeira vez ou precise de apoio para cumprir a sua obrigação regulamentar. Os preços dos EUAs respondem a mudanças na oferta, procura, política e no mercado de energia em geral. Ter uma visão clara dos seus requisitos esperados dá-lhe maior flexibilidade para considerar quando e como comprar, enquanto gere o seu orçamento e obrigações de conformidade. Os EUAs são uma parte cada vez mais importante da estratégia mais ampla de combustível e conformidade de um armador, o requisito de entrega aumentará para 100% das emissões em 2026, tornando-se não apenas uma transação anual. A KPI OceanConnect combina a experiência no mercado de carbono com uma compreensão da sua aquisição de combustível, operações e exposição regulamentar mais ampla. Isso permite-nos ajudá-lo a considerar as suas compras de EUA no contexto da sua estratégia geral de energia marítima. Clientes de EUA que regressam Reveja a sua posição de emissões de 2025, avalie quaisquer requisitos de EUA restantes e desenvolva a estratégia já em vigor. Clientes existentes de combustível marítimo Aproxime as suas estratégias de aquisição de combustível e EUA, apoiado por um parceiro com experiência em ambos os mercados. Novos clientes de EUA Obtenha uma visão clara dos volumes de EUA de que necessita, das opções de compra disponíveis e dos passos a seguir até à entrega. Empresas sem recursos dedicados ao EU ETS Aceda a suporte dedicado ao mercado de carbono sem a necessidade de uma equipa interna de conformidade ou negociação. Trabalhamos em conjunto com a sua equipa para calcular os requisitos e planear as compras, apoiar as transferências e facilitar o processo de entrega. A nossa equipa de Combustíveis Alternativos e Mercados de Carbono pode ajudá-lo a: A KPI OceanConnect apoia mais de 250 clientes com os seus requisitos de carbono e conformidade e negociou mais de 4,5 milhões de EUAs. Os nossos especialistas em mercado de carbono trabalham em conjunto com as nossas equipas globais de combustível marítimo, combinando conhecimento regulamentar, inteligência de mercado e décadas de experiência na negociação de energia marítima. Isso dá-lhe continuidade na aquisição de combustível, EU ETS e no cenário de transição energética em desenvolvimento. Quer precise de cumprir os requisitos deste ano ou desenvolver uma estratégia de compra a longo prazo, podemos fornecer o nível de suporte que se adapta à sua frota e organização. Para armadores e operadores cujos navios escalam portos da UE e do EEE, as obrigações do Sistema de Comércio de Emissões da União Europeia (EU ETS) e do FuelEU Maritime estão cada vez mais interligadas com as estratégias de aquisição de combustível. O combustível que queima molda a sua exposição ao carbono, e a sua estratégia de carbono molda qual combustível faz sentido comercial. Gerir múltiplas prioridades requer a compreensão dos riscos e oportunidades em jogo. Este FAQ aborda as perguntas que mais ouvimos dos operadores que tentam juntar estas peças numa estratégia coerente e económica. Sim. O combustível que escolhe abastecer tem um impacto direto no volume de EUAs que precisa de entregar, porque a sua obrigação de EUA é calculada a partir das emissões verificadas do seu navio. Combustíveis com menor teor de carbono, como biocombustíveis sustentáveis qualificados, podem reduzir esse valor de emissões, o que, por sua vez, reduz o número de EUAs que precisa de entregar. Em certos locais e momentos, a diferença de preço entre biocombustíveis e combustíveis convencionais diminuiu significativamente e, uma vez incluídos os custos de conformidade, a comparação do custo total pode favorecer o combustível alternativo. Isso destaca como a escolha do combustível agora precisa ser uma decisão mais ponderada, considerando tanto a conformidade quanto os custos. Isso é particularmente relevante porque a fase de implementação do EU ETS atinge 100% para as emissões geradas em 2026, com as licenças correspondentes a serem entregues em 2027. As emissões de metano e óxido nitroso também entram no esquema a partir de 2026, aumentando ainda mais a importância de cada decisão de combustível. Tomar decisões de combustível e EUA isoladamente corre o risco de incorrer numa fatura de conformidade mais alta do que o necessário. Ao avaliar as opções de combustível juntamente com os seus custos ajustados à conformidade, os operadores podem identificar onde uma mudança no tipo de combustível pode reduzir o custo total da viagem, mesmo que o próprio combustível tenha um preço diferente no papel. O EU ETS e o FuelEU Maritime são estruturas regulamentares separadas que podem aplicar-se ao mesmo navio, mas operam de forma diferente. O EU ETS é um mecanismo de precificação de carbono sob o qual as empresas de transporte marítimo devem entregar EUAs correspondentes às suas emissões verificadas e abrangidas. O requisito cobre 70% das emissões geradas em 2025 e cobrirá 100% das emissões geradas a partir de 2026. O FuelEU Maritime, por outro lado, estabelece limites progressivamente mais rigorosos para a intensidade de gases de efeito estufa do poço ao navio da energia utilizada a bordo, e para cumprir, os armadores precisarão de abastecer combustíveis mais limpos. A conformidade também pode ser alcançada através de acordos de pool, que permitem que o saldo positivo de conformidade de um navio compense o défice de outro. Na prática, isso significa que uma única decisão de combustível ou operacional pode afetar a sua posição em ambas as regulamentações. artigo.texto: CATL, Sungrow, Tesla and BYD are leading the global battery energy storage system market in 2026, but their leadership differs significantly across battery shipments, system integration, software, regional market share and mega-project execution. Battery storage has become one of the fastest-growing parts of global power infrastructure as utilities add batteries to integrate solar and wind, manage peak demand, provide grid flexibility and improve energy security. Global battery storage additions reached 108 GW in 2025, up 40 percent, according to the International Energy Agency. Installed capacity is now 11 times higher than in 2021. Around 80 percent of new capacity was utility-scale, while lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, accounted for approximately 90 percent of deployments. China represented around 60 percent of global additions, followed by the United States and Europe. Growth accelerated further in 2026. SNE Research reported global lithium-ion ESS battery shipments of 461.3 GWh in H1 2026, up 71 percent from 269.7 GWh a year earlier. Markets outside China accounted for 258.7 GWh, or 56 percent, exceeding half of global shipments for the first time. The global battery storage market is therefore moving rapidly beyond China, even though Chinese manufacturers continue to dominate battery-cell production and system integration. Which Company Is the World’s Largest Battery Storage Supplier? There is no single answer because the industry uses different measurements. CATL is the world’s largest ESS battery-cell supplier by H1 2026 shipments, delivering 125 GWh and capturing 27.1 percent of the global market. Sungrow ranks first in Wood Mackenzie’s 2026 Global BESS Integrator Comprehensive Ranking, which evaluates companies across technology, safety, R&D, supply chains, vertical integration, financial strength and other criteria. Tesla remains particularly strong in North America, while BYD combines cell manufacturing, system integration and large-scale project execution. The distinction matters because battery-cell manufacturing and BESS integration are different businesses. Global Top 10 Battery Storage Companies in 2026 Wood Mackenzie’s comprehensive 2026 BESS integrator ranking places the companies in the following order: The ranking demonstrates why BESS procurement is moving beyond battery price toward efficiency, safety, financial strength and lifetime performance. 1. Sungrow: World’s Top BESS Integrator Sungrow ranks first in Wood Mackenzie’s 2026 comprehensive assessment. Its advantage comes from combining battery systems with power conversion systems, controls and global project-integration capabilities. That is important because PCS efficiency, thermal management, grid-forming capability and system controls directly affect lifetime project economics. Sungrow also leads Europe’s BESS integrator market and has established a particularly strong position in the Middle East. 2. Tesla: Megapack and Software Create a Different Model Tesla ranks second globally in the comprehensive assessment and remains the leading BESS integrator in North America. Its Megapack strategy combines utility-scale battery hardware with Autobidder software, which can optimize battery participation in electricity markets. Tesla’s strength demonstrates why the storage battle extends beyond battery chemistry. Software capable of determining when to charge, discharge and participate in energy or ancillary-services markets can directly influence project revenue. 3. CATL: 125 GWh Makes It the ESS Battery-Cell Leader CATL dominates when measured by battery-cell shipments. The company shipped 125 GWh of ESS batteries during H1 2026, up 81 percent year over year, increasing its market share from 25.6 percent to 27.1 percent. For comparison, second-ranked EVE Energy shipped 48 GWh, while Hithium delivered 46.2 GWh. CATL therefore shipped more ESS batteries than the next two suppliers individually by a very wide margin. Its huge LFP manufacturing scale provides significant cost advantages, while continued investment in alternative technologies including sodium-ion could broaden its future storage portfolio. 4. BYD: Vertical Integration Meets Mega-Scale Storage BYD combines battery-cell manufacturing, electronics and complete storage-system integration. Its H1 2026 ESS cell shipments reached 35.7 GWh, giving it 7.7 percent global share. Its project footprint is equally important. BYD’s total contracted battery volume with Grenergy for Chile’s Oasis de Atacama project has reached 6.5 GWh across project phases. BYD is also gaining ground in Europe, where it moved from fifth to second among integrators. In the Middle East, BYD and Sungrow together captured 87 percent of the BESS market in 2025, demonstrating the scale of Chinese supplier expansion. 5. Envision Energy: Combining Renewables, Storage and Digital Control Envision and Trina Storage share fifth position in Wood Mackenzie’s comprehensive global ranking. Envision’s strategy extends beyond batteries because the company participates across renewable generation, storage and digital energy management. It ranked third in Asia-Pacific behind CRRC and HyperStrong. Combining wind, solar, storage and digital optimization could become valuable as utilities move toward integrated renewable-energy projects rather than procuring individual technologies separately. 6. Trina Storage: Utility-Scale Integration Trina Storage has developed its BESS position around the Elementa platform and utility-scale LFP projects. The company’s integration with the broader Trina Solar ecosystem also creates opportunities in solar-plus-storage. artigo.texto: Mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de distribuição de energia 380V 400V até 2035: crescimento se acelera com a demanda de data centers e renováveis Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V, o mercado chega a 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de distribuição de energia 380V 400V entra em uma fase de expansão sustentada, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa composta de 6–9% ao ano até 2035. Esse crescimento se apoia em três forças estruturais: a rápida expansão de data centers e de projetos de escala utilitária, a integração de energias renováveis e de sistemas de armazenamento em baterias e a eletrificação industrial em curso. A Ásia-Pacífico segue como centro de gravidade tanto da produção quanto do consumo, respondendo por quase metade da produção mundial e por parcela semelhante da demanda. As cadeias de suprimento regionais, porém, estão se redesenhando, com fabricantes ampliando capacidade de montagem na América do Norte e no Oriente Médio para reduzir prazos de entrega e atender a exigências de conteúdo local. O mercado também passa por uma atualização tecnológica: painéis de distribuição inteligentes, com medição integrada, proteção contra arco elétrico e monitoramento remoto, conquistam participação crescente em projetos de grande porte e alcançam prêmios de preço de 30–60% sobre as configurações básicas. Ao mesmo tempo, a volatilidade dos custos de matérias-primas e os prazos prolongados de componentes representam riscos para margens e fornecimento. Este relatório oferece uma perspectiva baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, arquitetura da demanda, dinâmica competitiva e tendências regionais até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de distribuição de energia 380V 400V prevê crescimento constante até 2035, com a demanda global avançando a uma taxa composta de 6–9% ao ano. Essa projeção pressupõe continuidade dos investimentos em infraestrutura de rede, projetos de energia renovável e data centers, além de despesas de capital industrial moderadas. A Ásia-Pacífico continuará sendo o maior mercado, sustentada por polos manufatureiros na China, na Índia e no Sudeste Asiático, mas o crescimento também se acelerará na América do Norte e na Europa, à medida que a infraestrutura envelhecida for modernizada e a digitalização das redes de baixa tensão ganhar ritmo. O índice de mercado (2025=100) deve alcançar 185 em 2035, refletindo uma quase duplicação da atividade de mercado no período de previsão. Entre as principais incertezas estão a volatilidade dos preços de matérias-primas, sobretudo cobre e aço, e o ritmo de harmonização das normas entre as regiões. Ainda assim, os vetores fundamentais da demanda — eletrificação, descarbonização e digitalização — são robustos, e espera-se que o mercado supere o crescimento industrial mais amplo. A migração para equipamentos de distribuição inteligentes continuará a remodelar portfólios de produtos e posicionamento competitivo, com ganho de participação para fornecedores capazes de oferecer soluções integradas, em conformidade com as normas e com entrega rápida. Vetores e restrições da demanda Principais vetores de demanda - Expansão acelerada de data centers e infraestrutura de nuvem, que exige distribuição de energia 380V/400V confiável para servidores, refrigeração e sistemas de backup. - Integração de energias renováveis e armazenamento em baterias, em que usinas solares e eólicas precisam de distribuição CA de baixa tensão dedicada para inversores e cargas auxiliares. - Eletrificação e automação industrial, com fábricas migrando para a manufatura inteligente e substituindo processos a combustível fóssil por alternativas elétricas. - Investimentos em modernização e resiliência da rede, sobretudo na América do Norte e na Europa, para substituir equipamentos envelhecidos e melhorar a confiabilidade. - Digitalização da distribuição de baixa tensão, com disjuntores e sistemas de monitoramento habilitados para IoT especificados em 20–30% dos grandes projetos. - Regionalização das cadeias de suprimento, levando fabricantes a estabelecer montagem local na América do Norte e no Oriente Médio para atender às regras de conteúdo local. Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - Volatilidade dos custos de matérias-primas, especialmente cobre e aço galvanizado, que pressiona margens e complica licitações de preço fixo. - Prazos prolongados para componentes especializados, como disjuntores em caixa moldada, limitando a produção de integradores de pequeno e médio porte. - Divergências de normas de segurança e desempenho entre regiões (IEC, UL, AS/NZS), elevando os custos de qualificação para fornecedores globais. - Escassez de mão de obra qualificada para instalação e comissionamento, sobretudo em projetos de renováveis e data centers em rápido crescimento. - Concorrência intensa de produtores de baixo custo, especialmente nos segmentos de linha padrão, limitando o poder de precificação dos fornecedores premium. artigo.texto: Atmos Renewables, an Australian renewableenergy firm, has reached financial close on two Capacity Investment Scheme-backed projects in Australia: the 400 MW/1,600 MWh Teebar BESS and 470 MW Parron Maam Marang Wind Farm. Atmos Renewables is the Australian renewable energy business of Igneo Infrastructure Partners, developing, owning and operating utility-scale wind, solar and battery storage assets. The four-hour Teebar BESS will be built beside Powerlink’s Teebar Creek substation in Queensland’s Fraser Coast region. Parron Maam Marang will be developed in Western Australia’s Wheatbelt and supply electricity to Synergy under a long-term PPA. Together with the 100 MW/400 MWh Merredin BESS, Atmos has taken 970 MW of CIS-backed capacity through financial close over 16 months. Atmos will retain ownership of both projects during construction and operate them after completion. Its national portfolio now exceeds 1.5 GW of operating and under-construction wind, solar and storage capacity. artigo.texto: FLORIDA – The race for Florida governor is drawing sharp contrasts on some of the state’s most pressing issues. Democratic candidate David Jolly and Republican Rep. Byron Donalds sat down separately this week to answer questions on artificial intelligence, hyperscale data centers and Amendment 3, a property tax relief measure heading to voters next month. Here is where each candidate stands: Recommended Videos AI Data Centers Jolly said he would issue a moratorium on hyperscale data centers on his first day in office, arguing the industry is rushing into a state with a favorable regulatory and campaign finance environment before the public health and environmental questions have been answered. “This is moving too quickly,” Jolly said. “Big tech and big data are rushing into a relatively unregulated or favorably regulated environment.” Jolly pointed to a data center community in Northern Virginia where, he said, four children had been treated for respiratory conditions, one had been hospitalized, and several had been treated for hearing conditions. He said nearly 75% of Florida voters oppose the facilities. “Florida’s voters are saying, don’t do this. And I’ve said, I’ll issue a moratorium on my very first day in office,” Jolly said. Donalds took a different approach, saying the decision belongs to local governments — not the state. “County commissioners issue building permits, not governors,” Donalds said. “Local communities do.” Donalds said state law, signed by Gov. Ron DeSantis, already puts siting decisions in the hands of local communities. At the state level, he said his administration would focus on two guarantees: utility bills would not increase because of data centers, and fresh water would be protected through existing water use permit requirements administered by water management districts. Donalds also noted a study commissioned by the state is due back June 1, 2027, and said he would release it publicly. “We are going to maintain that,” Donalds said of the existing permitting framework. “This is not a new phenomenon.” Artificial Intelligence Jolly called himself an AI optimist but said the technology’s integration — not its promise — is the critical issue. He cited concerns about job displacement, children’s privacy and the role of AI in classrooms, arguing teachers should use AI as a tool, not be replaced by it. “AI should not replace a teacher,” Jolly said. “But I think teachers could benefit from AI.” He also cited what he described as a corrupt campaign finance system quieting public concerns. “The public is saying, hey, pump the brakes, slow down. Even the inventors of AI at times are saying, slow it down,” Jolly said. On job displacement, Jolly drew a comparison to trade adjustment assistance programs created during NAFTA and CAFTA, saying Florida may need a similar retraining and assistance framework if the federal government fails to act. Donalds said AI is already embedded in everyday life and cannot be put back in a box. “If you got rid of the models at the top four or five companies, there’s probably 500 young computer scientists and engineers who are already making up their own model,” Donalds said. He said Florida should focus on protecting children, safeguarding name, image and likeness rights, and empowering parents. He also pointed to commercial space development on the Space Coast as an example of AI-powered economic opportunity, calling it a potential $1 trillion industry generating high-paying jobs across multiple fields. “The question is, how do we protect families? How do we protect communities and how do we protect children?” Donalds said. Amendment 3 Both candidates acknowledged the property tax burden on Florida residents, but they land on opposite sides of the measure. Jolly said he anticipates voting no on Amendment 3, aligning with sheriffs and law enforcement groups who have warned the measure would cut funding for public safety services. “That’s essentially what Amendment 3 is gonna do. It’s gonna defund law enforcement along with critical services that communities need,” Jolly said. He said the measure was rushed through without a sufficient funding backstop and noted that Gov. DeSantis, who initially proposed a version of the idea, is not actively campaigning for it. Jolly said he would instead pursue targeted relief — a homestead exemption of up to $250,000 for first-time homebuyers, income-based relief for seniors, and returning expanded exemption authority to local governments. “Let’s target first-time homebuying tax relief,” Jolly said, noting the average age of a first-time homebuyer in Florida has risen from 28 to roughly 40 or 41 years old. Donalds said he supports Amendment 3, arguing property taxes on Florida residents have effectively doubled over the past seven years. “It’s not our money. It belongs to the citizen. It belongs to the taxpayer,” Donalds said. He said the amendment’s language requires public safety to be funded first before any cuts take effect. For fiscally constrained counties, he proposed a dedicated funding formula so those governments would not need to lobby Tallahassee for help. He also argued larger counties had the option to roll back tax rates as property values rose over the past six years and chose not to. “Local governments have to live within their means, the same way the state government has to live within our means,” Donalds said.

artigo.texto: SPOKANE, Wash. — The "Aquifers over AI" rally in Spokane on Sunday called for a statewide pause on new data centers, as organizers raised concerns about the impacts on water use and strain on local infrastructure. The event on Sunday was part of the Statewide Day of Action, where activists from across the state hosted rallies in many cities, demanding a statewide moratorium on new data center construction. Organizers said the push centered on protecting groundwater resources because they believed growing AI infrastructure could affect the city's aquifer. About 100 people attended the rally. Guest speakers from environmental nonprofit organizations also took part. The group started at the Riverfront Park Rotary Fountain, marched past City Hall and the Public Works building, and crossed the Monroe Street Bridge. Organizers said they wanted more transparency about the strain data centers place on regional infrastructure, noise pollution, and calls for more local and statewide moratoriums on new data centers. One of the organizers said the effort needed to go beyond Spokane and involve other communities. "Like, sure, it's great to pass in the city, but they're not going to build one here. It's going to be in the county. It's going to be in another city. Like this is why it's important that we build a coalition. We work with other jurisdictions; we work statewide to pass this moratorium," said Zenthia Peterson. Organizers also said the Spokane River was running the driest it had ever been and argued new data centers could make that worse. They said they hoped the turnout would send a message in support of a statewide moratorium against new data centers.

artigo.texto: Volkswagen Rewires Battery Supply and Model Lineup as Margins Hit a Wall Published on 10/04/2026 at 19:20 | Editorial boerse-global.de Volkswagen is pressing ahead with a sweeping overhaul of how it builds cars and where it sources their batteries, even as the financial picture darkens. The Wolfsburg group has locked in a trio of battery joint ventures, signaled the arrival of an electric Tiguan, and opened a new round of labor talks — all while its shares scrape the bottom of a 52-week range. Three joint ventures, one trimmed stake Under an agreement dated September 28, Volkswagen Group, its in-house battery unit PowerCo SE and China's Gotion High-tech will establish three separate joint companies. The ventures will turn out LFP battery cells and cathode material at plants in Valencia, Spain; Šurany, Slovakia; and Kenitra, Morocco. The partners also plan to pool procurement and sales efforts across Europe. As part of the same arrangement, Volkswagen signed a binding deal to offload 5.3 percent of its holding in Gotion. The group will keep a meaningful stake once the transaction closes. Paris as a stage The battery pacts sit alongside a broader push to shore up its European base. On Thursday, ahead of an industry gathering in France, Volkswagen unveiled its "For Europe" initiative, pledging to strengthen European supply chains and safeguard future-proof jobs. Investment will concentrate on electric mobility, battery technology, software and artificial intelligence. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Volkswagen? A political and media exchange is set for Paris on October 11, followed the next day by the Paris Motor Show, where the Volkswagen, Audi, Škoda, CUPRA and Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles brands will roll out new models. Back home, the company confirmed the October debut of the ID. Tiguan, with the model's actual market launch slated for early 2027. Contracts on the table Labor relations form the other front. On Wednesday, management gave notice on several collective agreements effective December 31, 2026, while explicitly exempting the future collective agreement that guarantees job security. Revision talks have already begun, with further sessions with IG Metall scheduled for the second half of October. A warning that reset expectations These moves are unfolding against a sharply weaker backdrop. In mid-September, Volkswagen cut its full-year 2026 guidance, projecting revenue of roughly EUR 315 billion and an operating margin of up to 1 percent. The company had previously targeted a margin of 4.0 to 5.5 percent. Management blamed restructuring costs, a tough market in China and a non-cash write-down of about EUR 6 billion on Porsche. Sentiment took a further hit roughly a week ago when Germany's KBA federal transport authority ordered a recall over a potentially corrosion-prone steering screw. Volkswagen at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Analysts trim their targets The revisions have rippled through brokerages. On September 21, Kepler Cheuvreux's Michael Raab downgraded the stock from "Buy" to "Hold" and cut his price target to EUR 80 from EUR 92, citing the reduced valuation headroom after the profit warning. That same day, DZ Bank's Michael Punzet lowered his fair value to EUR 73 from EUR 75, keeping a "Hold" rating and pointing to the reduced margin forecast for the year and more demanding targets through the end of the decade. A stock near its floor The market has taken notice. The shares are down 35 percent since the start of the year, and on Friday they closed at EUR 67.60 — barely above the fresh 52-week low of EUR 67.22 touched during the session. Investors will get a fuller read on October 29, when Volkswagen publishes its interim report for the first nine months. artigo.texto: Pointo bets on e-auto, BESS, second-life battery segments to drive growth Lithium-ion battery startup Pointo plans to raise ₹70-100 crore to build an automated refurbishment unit and expand its distribution network Press Trust of India Kolkata WebinarsNew Deep DiveNew Explore Business Standard Lithium-ion battery distribution and service network startup Pointo is betting big on the expanding e-auto segment, battery storage systems (BESS) and second-life products to bolster its revenue, while actively engaging with investors to raise Rs 70-100 crore for its next expansion phase, a top company official said. The city-based startup, which previously raised Rs 6.2 crore in a seed funding round led by Equirus InnovateX Fund, plans to deploy the fresh capital to build an automated, large-scale refurbishment unit and expand its ground distribution network across the country. The company has seen its revenue run rate jump to Rs 80 crore in FY26 from about Rs 3 crore in FY24, and expects to close the current financial year at a revenue of Rs 150 crore, Founder & CEO of Pointo Riki Biswas told PTI. Founded in 2023 by Biswas, a chemical engineer from IIT Guwahati, along with three co-founders, Pointo aims to build a closed-loop supply chain across battery deployment, buyback, refurbishment and second-life applications. By eliminating high upfront costs and enabling instant access through financing tie-ups with non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), the company aims to redefine how India powers its electric vehicles (EVs). Biswas said the company has tied up with lithium-ion battery original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) for co-branding and marketing, alongside multiple NBFC partnerships to provide finance-ready lithium-ion batteries to e-rickshaw drivers and fleets. The startup currently serves 25,000 customers through more than 22 physical hubs spread across six states: West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Punjab. It is now looking to strengthen its micro-distribution network to reach Tier II and Tier III towns. "We are building a strong distribution network through a hub and spoke model, building a closed-loop supply chain across battery deployment, buyback, refurbishment and second-life applications. We are currently working in the e-rickshaw segment, which itself is a large market estimated at around 50 lakh vehicles. We will ramp up our presence in this segment," Biswas told PTI. "We also see a huge opportunity in the L5 E-auto, BESS and second-life products. We already have an existing distribution network, and we are looking to expand our network in the existing markets. This will enable us to tap into this growing demand efficiently," he added. Highlighting the market potential in the e-auto and four-wheeler segment, Biswas noted that starting next year, close to 8,000 to 10,000 electric autos are expected to come up for battery replacement, generating substantial demand for new lithium-ion batteries. The batteries retrieved during replacement will also serve as a key raw material source for second-life applications and new battery minerals. Pointo plans to convert end-of-life batteries into lower-use products such as home inverters for resale, helping shore up revenues while playing a crucial role in the circular supply chain. "We have a 20,000 sq ft R&D and refurbishment centre, and with a ready customer base, our next phase is to build an automated, large-scale refurbishment unit. We are in active discussion with investors to raise close to Rs 70-100 crore to build the refurbishment unit and expand the ground network," Biswas said. artigo.texto: Kenya is set to receive KSh590 million in European Union climate funding to strengthen the systems used to monitor, report and verify carbon-market activities and national climate action, as the country moves to establish a more structured framework for participating in international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. The announcement was made in Nairobi on 5 October 2026 during the launch of the Kenya Guide for Strategic Engagement in Carbon Markets 2026, placing market integrity and institutional capacity at the centre of Kenya’s next phase of carbon-market development. EU Deputy Ambassador to Kenya Ondřej Šimíček said the funding, equivalent to about €4 million, would support Kenya’s monitoring, reporting and validation systems for both mitigation activities and national climate commitments. The support comes as Kenya seeks to create greater certainty for investors and project developers while ensuring that international transfers of carbon-related mitigation outcomes do not undermine the country’s own emissions-reduction commitments. The new Guide provides the institutional bridge between Kenya’s existing carbon-market regulations and the practical decisions required when projects seek to participate in international markets. Developed by the Government of Kenya with technical support from the Global Green Growth Institute’s Carbon Transaction Facility, it establishes principles, assessment criteria and implementation arrangements for evaluating and authorising carbon-market activities. It is intended to complement the Climate Change (Carbon Markets) Regulations, 2024, which provide Kenya’s underlying legal and institutional framework for carbon projects. One of the most significant elements of the framework is its approach to the volume of mitigation outcomes Kenya can authorise for international transfer. The Guide establishes a national carbon budget for trading, effectively placing a ceiling on the quantity of mitigation outcomes that can be transferred internationally while protecting the country’s ability to meet its Nationally Determined Contribution. Independent analysis of the July 2026 Guide puts the cumulative ceiling at approximately 10 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent through 2030. That limit is important because Article 6 transactions involve more than the sale of conventional carbon credits. Article 6.2 provides rules for countries cooperating through internationally transferred mitigation outcomes, or ITMOs, while requiring accounting arrangements designed to prevent double counting. Article 6.4 establishes a United Nations-supervised mechanism for generating and trading carbon credits, while Article 6.8 covers non-market approaches to international cooperation. For Kenya, this means the government must be able to determine which mitigation outcomes can be transferred abroad, record those transfers and account for them against its national climate commitments. The country’s 2024 carbon-market regulations already provide for authorisation of ITMO transfers and require corresponding adjustments where applicable. They also require transferred mitigation outcomes to be recorded in the National Carbon Registry. The development of the registry has consequently become an important component of Kenya’s carbon-market architecture. The Kenya National Carbon Registry was formally launched in February 2026 and is designed to track, verify and manage carbon credits and internationally transferred mitigation outcomes. The registry is managed by the National Environment Management Authority (NEMA), which also serves as Kenya’s Designated National Authority for Article 6 and other carbon markets. The registry is intended to address one of the fundamental risks facing carbon markets: whether emissions reductions or removals can be uniquely identified, tracked and accounted for throughout their lifecycle. NEMA has said the registry will support transparency, prevent double counting and double issuance, and provide a national platform for recording carbon-market projects, authorisations and mitigation outcomes. The Guide adds another layer of decision-making by establishing clearer criteria for projects seeking government approval. It introduces a structured process for engagement and prioritises activities that align with Kenya’s climate and development objectives. The framework also places greater emphasis on environmental and social safeguards, stakeholder engagement, benefit sharing and the broader value that carbon projects can create beyond the sale of credits. That shift has implications for the investment market. Carbon projects are increasingly being assessed not only according to the number of credits they can potentially generate, but also according to whether their emissions reductions are measurable, additional, traceable and compatible with national climate policy. Weak monitoring systems or uncertain ownership and accounting rules can increase transaction risks and make international buyers more cautious. For Kenya, strengthening monitoring, reporting and verification therefore has an economic dimension. Credible systems can reduce uncertainty for investors, improve the ability of buyers to assess projects and provide government with stronger oversight of mitigation activities taking place within its borders. The EU funding announced in Nairobi is intended to strengthen precisely these institutional capabilities. The development also builds on a longer Kenya-EU climate partnership. European support has been directed towards renewable energy, climate resilience, sustainable agriculture and climate-governance systems, while Kenya has been developing its own institutional capacity for carbon-market participation. The EU has also supported wider climate and green-growth initiatives that seek to mobilise private investment alongside public and development finance. artigo.texto: Carbon tax deferment gives ministry more time to finalise regulatory, policy framework, says Arthur KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The deferment of the carbon tax implementation is aligned with the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry’s efforts to establish a complete regulatory and policy framework before enforcing emission caps. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the government decided to delay the tax, originally planned for this year, following global geopolitical developments that led to volatile energy prices, providing affected industries with a necessary buffer. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. That’s why we’ve been successful in launching the National Carbon Market Policy and I hope that we can table the Climate Change Act soon. “Once that is up, then we have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including the regulation, enforcement, the regulatory powers to give us to set the emission ceiling, and then we can know anything above the ceiling, then the carbon tax will come into place as a penalty to the polluters. “So, we’re not looking at this year for the carbon tax,” he said. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. He added that while operators need adequate time for feasibility studies and modifications, strict progress is required to qualify for temporary extensions. The session, titled “Building A Resilient Malaysia: Environment, Climate And Our Future”, was moderated by Bernama chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai. Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, as well as members of the local and foreign media based in Malaysia. artigo.texto: Tesla deliveries top consensus, but energy storage deployments miss estimates Published: 12:40 05 Oct 2026 EDT Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA) delivered 487,000 vehicles in the third quarter, beating consensus estimates by 5% and extending the rebound in vehicle deliveries, according to UBS Securities. The electric vehicle maker’s deliveries rose 1% from the previous quarter but fell 2% year on year, with Model 3 and Model Y deliveries increasing 2% quarter on quarter and declining 1% year on year. UBS maintained its 'neutral' rating on Tesla and a $385 price target. UBS said the delivery result was positive, although expectations among investors had risen ahead of the release and may have reached 470,000 to 490,000 vehicles. The analyst said Tesla’s vehicle deliveries remained strong in some newer markets and exports, supported by production from its Shanghai facility. Tesla produced 464,000 vehicles in the quarter, up 3% from the previous quarter and 4% year on year, leaving production below deliveries and reducing estimated inventory days to 18 from 22. The weaker element of the release was energy storage, with deployments of 13.7 gigawatt-hours, up 1% quarter on quarter and 10% year on year but below the 15.9 gigawatt-hours consensus estimate. UBS said energy deployments were lumpy and difficult to forecast, but the shortfall could have a modest impact on its model because the business generates above-average gross margins. The analyst estimated the energy miss could reduce earnings by about $0.03, all else equal, leaving the overall delivery release with a mix of positive and negative factors.

artigo.texto: Companies Strengthen Position in Data Center Market Through Long-Term Chiller Partnership Supporting More Than 5GW of AI Data Center Capacity News Summary - LG Electronics has secured a long-term supply agreement with AIR Control Concepts to provide advanced cooling solutions for AI data centers in North America. - The agreement supports a large-scale, multi-year chiller supply program supporting data centers with more than 5GW of capacity. - This milestone reflects AIR's confidence in LG's cooling technologies to meet the demanding standards required for hyperscale data center infrastructure, positioning LG as a key supplier in this market. - For AIR, the partnership reinforces its position as one of North America's fastest-growing AI data center infrastructure platforms. NORFOLK, Va., Oct. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LG Electronics USA has signed a major supply agreement with AIR Control Concepts (AIR), the largest global platform of leading HVAC, electrical, service, and controls companies, to provide advanced chillers for data centers in the United States and Canada. The long-term contract builds on AIR's role as a leading AI data center (AIDC) platform provider and accelerates LG's expansion into the global AIDC cooling market, addressing the rapidly growing demand for high-efficiency thermal management solutions in AI infrastructure. Securing AI Infrastructure Partnership with Leading Data Center Developers Under the agreement, LG will supply advanced chillers supporting large-scale AI data center projects exceeding 5GW of capacity in North America. AIR oversees mega-scale infrastructure projects across major North American data center hubs, serving leading global data center operators as key customers. The LG Air-Cooled Centrifugal Chiller designed for AI data centers incorporates refrigerant free-cooling technology, using cool outdoor air to lower the compressor cooling load. Based on LG's internal simulation, refrigerant free-cooling can consume approximately 30 percent less energy annually than waterside free-cooling.1 This contract demonstrates that LG's cooling solutions meet AIR's stringent technical and reliability requirements for its hyperscale data center projects. Moving beyond single-project bids, the agreement establishes LG as a core infrastructure partner supporting the growth of AI data centers in North America. For AIR, the partnership reinforces its position as one of North America's fastest-growing AI data center infrastructure platforms. As data center customers race to bring new capacity online, AIR is scaling the operational depth and supplier relationships needed to deliver mission-critical cooling infrastructure on schedule and at the standard the industry now requires. Targeting Rapid Growth in the Global AIDC Market The expansion of LG's AI data center cooling business draws on six decades of HVAC engineering experience in high-reliability environments such as nuclear power plants and large hospitals. Building on recent successes in supplying cooling solutions to hyperscale AI data centers in North America, LG is also expanding its global footprint with key data center projects in the Middle East and Indonesia. By leveraging the integrated capabilities of the broader LG Group to offer comprehensive cooling solutions, the company aims to drive mid- to long-term revenue growth. The global AI data center market presents significant growth opportunities. According to Fortune Business Insights, the market is expected to grow by approximately 26 percent annually, reaching $133.5 billion by 2034. In its second-quarter 2026 earnings report, LG highlighted that first-half orders for data center cooling solutions exceeded $428 million, and the company expects orders to reach several billion dollars by year-end. The company expects to achieve its 2027 chiller business revenue target of approximately $680 million (1 trillion Korean won) ahead of schedule.2 Leveraging Complementary Capabilities to Address Exploding Demand "This agreement reflects the confidence data center customers place in AIR to deliver mission-critical infrastructure at a scale and pace the industry has never seen before," said Brad Hobbs, Chief Executive Officer of AIR Control Concepts. "LG's high-efficiency chiller technology gives us a proven platform we can deploy with confidence across our AI data center portfolio, and this agreement positions AIR to support our customers' growth for years to come." "As heat management in AI data centers emerges as a major global priority, LG aims to be a major player in the global AIDC cooling market," said James Lee, president of the LG Electronics ES Company. "We will achieve this through our differentiated technology, including our high-efficiency chillers, and our rapidly expanding experience in supplying leading big tech companies." "We're excited to deepen our partnership with LG at exactly the moment our industry needs it most," said Hayden Bland, President of AIR Control Concepts. "Data center operators are looking for partners who can deliver mission-critical reliability, capacity and certainty at scale. Together with LG, we're building the technology, manufacturing capacity and support infrastructure to meet that need. For data center customers planning their next generation of infrastructure, now is the time to engage with us." "Data center cooling represents a key pillar of LG's global growth strategy, and this major supply agreement with AIR marks an inflection point for LG's North American chiller business," said Don Kwack, CEO, LG Electronics North America. "This alliance leverages LG's proven cooling innovations and AIR's strong position with U.S. data center developers at a critical time for reliable AI infrastructure expansion." 1 Based on LG's internal simulation of a single 1,750 kW unit operating at 100 percent cooling capacity under climate conditions in the Seoul metropolitan area. artigo.texto: TONGANOXIE, Kan. — — About 150 people gathered in Tonganoxie Sunday with a unified message: responsible AI development matters. Watch Ryan's 5 p.m. report in the video player below. The community turned out to hear the latest on Project Bluestem, a proposed 1,000-acre hyperscale data center campus paired with a gas power plant, as residents continue to push back against a project they say has no place in their community. "These corporations don't care about you," Matt Beat, aka "Mr. Beat," the keynote speaker, influencer, and YouTuber, told listeners. The feeling is mutual in Tonganoxie. KSHB 41 News Reporter Ryan Gamboa recently covered a special meeting with Leavenworth County commissioners, where commissioners Dove and Smith were absent. In the meeting, more than 1,000 neighbors argued why Project Bluestem doesn't belong in their community. Tyler Romans, a Tonganoxie resident, says the fight reflects something far deeper than a land use dispute. "Tonganoxie and the fight against this data center is really a microcosm for the broader issues in American politics," Romans said. "We are David fighting Goliath. And Goliath has a million dollars and two million lawyers, and we're over here trying to scrape by." Tensions continue to flare in Leavenworth County over the county government's inaction on the Project Bluestem data center project. Romans told Gamboa he's frustrated that elected leaders are advocating for these projects. At the state level, he placed blame on state lawmakers for passing Senate Bill 98, which is home to tax breaks and data center developers. "The failure of that state and county government and local government to protect us. We elected these people to guide our communities into prosperity, but there is no guidance. It's a sellout," Romans said. The political stakes sharpened last week when the Leavenworth County Commission voted 3-to-2 to remove Mike Stieben as commissioner chair. The title is merely ceremonial. But it comes with a responsibility. Commissioner Jeff Culbertson moved to make the change during the meeting. "I'd like to bring up something that I've been asked to do for months... take a vote of the board on changing out the chair, " Jeff Culbertson, a Leavenworth County commissioner, brought up during the Sept. 30 meeting. Stieben has been a vocal opponent of the data center project, along with his constituents. Commissioners Culbertson, Dove, and Reid pointed out Stieben's actions are the cause. "It's the Mike Stieben show," Reid pointed out. Stieben pushed back on the commissioners' motion to oust him, claiming the motivation stems from them wanting to approve the data center development. "You're going to saddle Tonganoxie with this project. That's what this is completely about," Commissioner Stieben said on Wednesday. Stieben told Gamboa on Sunday that the removal won't silence him and it may have backfired. "It was an attempt to silence me, but um not gonna be silenced, I'm not gonna be silenced. I represent Tonganoxie, I represent Linwood, we're gonna continue to represent them," Stieben said. "There's a lot more freedom not being the Chair, and maybe they should've considered that because my entire focus until January is to focus on this project for my constituents." For Romans, the political fallout is a call to action at the ballot box. "When we see our leadership fail us, that is when we need to start talking about voting these people out. That was a huge primary driver in the primaries that just happened, and it's going to be a huge driver in the elections in November," Romans said. Rebecca Davis, organizer for the Tongie Data Center Watchdog, says the movement is gaining ground. "Definitely the resistance is growing. 7 out of 10 Americans don't want a data center in their community. That lines up pretty good here in Tonganoxie," Davis explained. Davis added that the data center debate needs to go deeper than economics. "What is AI? How can it ethically fit into our society? I think it has great benefits in the medical field, but we don't need AI slop taking over everything," Davis said. "We don't need mass loss of jobs. So, ethical AI is amazing, but hitting the gas on hyper-scale data centers, just do it as fast as you can, just no." For Romans, the stakes of the movement dying couldn't be higher, and more personal. "We keep fighting because there is no plan B for us, because we're going to live here no matter what. I would much rather live in the town I fell in love with than an industrial hellscape," Romans said. Commissioner Stieben still has no doubt how it's all going to end. "I believe we're going to win this," Stieben said. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI.
