artigo.texto: Not true we " didn't have the language". My 47 year old has it. I also worked in the industry in which they were diagnosed. The criteria has been loosened. Dear Bess, ADHD didn’t exist when I was younger. Now all three of my grandkids have been diagnosed with it. I’m not even sure I believe it’s real. How do I deal with this as a grandmother? Signed, Sceptical Nan Sceptical Nan, I want to start by taking your observation seriously, because I think it’s more reasonable than you’ve perhaps been given credit for. You’re right that almost nobody was being diagnosed with ADHD when you were raising your own children. That’s not a false memory. It’s a genuine, well-documented fact. So let’s separate two things, because I think they’ve become tangled together in your mind, understandably. The first is whether ADHD, as a real, biological difference in how a brain works, actually exists. The second is why so many more children are being diagnosed with it now than in your day. Those are genuinely different questions, and I think the honest answer to the second one is actually what’s fuelling your doubt about the first. Here’s what the research genuinely shows. ADHD is one of the most heritable conditions in psychiatry, with studies putting the genetic contribution at around 80 per cent. Twin studies have found identical twins share an ADHD diagnosis around 81 per cent of the time, compared to just 29 per cent for fraternal twins, which is about as strong a signal of a real, biological basis as you’ll find for almost any condition. Researchers have also identified specific genes involved in dopamine regulation that show up consistently in people with ADHD. This isn’t a fashionable label invented to explain away ordinary childhood behaviour. It’s a genuine, inherited difference in brain function, sitting alongside things like eye colour or a family tendency toward migraines, mostly out of anyone’s control. What has genuinely changed is who gets identified. The diagnostic criteria themselves have been broadened more than once, most notably in 1994 and again in 2013, when the age by which symptoms needed to first appear was pushed out from seven to twelve. Awareness among doctors, teachers and parents has grown enormously. And it’s now well understood that girls and quieter, less disruptive children were routinely missed for decades, because the original picture of ADHD was built almost entirely around loud, hyperactive little boys. A very recent Danish study of more than two million children, published just this week, found that children diagnosed with ADHD today actually resemble the general population more closely than those diagnosed a decade ago, suggesting the diagnostic net has genuinely widened to catch milder, previously overlooked presentations, not that the condition has been invented from nothing. So my honest answer, Nan, is this: the condition was almost certainly always there. What’s changed is that we’ve finally built the tools, and the willingness, to actually see it. Now, the more important question. What do you actually do with this, as a grandmother? Here’s where I’d gently steer you. Your grandchildren’s parents have presumably gone through a genuine, often lengthy assessment process to arrive at three separate diagnoses. That’s not something families pursue lightly, and it’s worth trusting that process, even if the framework itself is unfamiliar to you. Your scepticism, if it’s shared openly with your grandchildren or spoken about within earshot, risks landing as a quiet message that their diagnosis, and by extension, their struggles, aren’t real or aren’t taken seriously. That’s a genuinely painful thing for a child to absorb from someone they love, even unintentionally. What I’d suggest instead is holding your questions privately, or raising them directly and respectfully with their parents, rather than with the children themselves. Ask what you can do to support them, practically, day to day. Ask what helps and what doesn’t. You don’t need to fully understand the science to be a genuinely steady, loving presence in their lives, and honestly, that steadiness matters far more to a child than whether their grandmother has fully come around on the diagnostic criteria. One last thought, Sceptical Nan. You raised children in a world that simply didn’t have this language yet. That’s not a failing on your part, and it doesn’t make your instincts wrong to question something new. But I’d encourage you to let your genuine curiosity lead here, rather than your doubt. Ask questions. Read a little. You may find, as so many grandparents eventually do, that what you’re really looking at isn’t something new at all, just something that finally has a name. Have a question for Bess? Write to her at community@startsat60.com with “Dear Bess” in the subject line. Join the conversation. Comments are reviewed before they appear. artigo.texto: Mercado global de baterias de base biológica: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado global de baterias de base biológica até 2035: crescimento impulsionado por metas corporativas de ESG e aplicações críticas de segurança Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de baterias de base biológica, o mercado entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de baterias de base biológica está deixando a fase de validação em laboratório para entrar na implantação comercial inicial, abrindo nichos defensáveis em que biodegradabilidade, não toxicidade e segurança reforçada compensam as atuais limitações de densidade energética e potência. Diferentemente da cadeia de suprimentos intensiva em minerais das baterias de íons de lítio, os gargalos críticos desse mercado estão no fornecimento de bio-precursores de alta pureza, como celulose, quitosana e lignina, e no estabelecimento de rotas de bioprocessamento escaláveis. A demanda se divide entre aplicações sensíveis a custo e de grande volume, como embalagens inteligentes e eletrônicos descartáveis, e segmentos premium, como implantes médicos e sensores ambientais, em que credenciais de segurança e sustentabilidade justificam um prêmio de preço. A integração de sistemas continua sendo um obstáculo, pois as células de base biológica frequentemente exigem sistemas de gerenciamento de bateria sob medida, adaptados aos seus perfis únicos de carga e descarga. Os ventos regulatórios favoráveis do REACH e das restrições a PFAS são contrabalançados pela ausência de padrões de desempenho unificados, o que retarda a qualificação junto a compradores avessos ao risco. Os papéis geográficos vão se cristalizando, com regiões fortes em biotecnologia emergindo como polos de P&D e mercados com regras ambientais rigorosas formando os primeiros núcleos de demanda. Este relatório analisa o mercado de 2012 a 2025 e projeta o período até 2035, oferecendo uma visão estruturada da demanda de implantação, do posicionamento tecnológico e da dinâmica competitiva. O cenário-base para o mercado de baterias de base biológica até 2035 prevê uma transição da prototipagem de nicho para a comercialização em escala, embora o crescimento permaneça concentrado em aplicações especializadas, e não na substituição massiva das baterias de íons de lítio. Espera-se que o mercado cresça a uma taxa composta de crescimento anual de 8,2% entre 2026 e 2035, alcançando um índice de mercado de 220 em 2035 (2025=100). Esse crescimento se apoia em três forças estruturais: primeiro, o endurecimento das regulamentações ambientais sobre descarte de baterias e materiais perigosos, sobretudo na Europa e na América do Norte, obrigará os fabricantes de equipamentos originais a buscar alternativas para dispositivos de baixa potência e descartáveis; segundo, as metas corporativas de ESG impulsionarão a compra de soluções de armazenamento sustentáveis para redes de IoT, monitoramento ambiental e energia de reserva em locais sensíveis; e terceiro, aplicações críticas de segurança nos setores médico, de defesa e em instalações protegidas adotarão químicas de base biológica onde os riscos de fuga térmica das baterias convencionais são inaceitáveis. No entanto, o cenário-base não pressupõe nenhum avanço na densidade energética que torne as baterias de base biológica competitivas para armazenamento em escala na rede ou para veículos elétricos antes de 2035. O desenvolvimento da cadeia de suprimentos se concentrará em garantir bio-precursores consistentes e de alta pureza e em escalar o bioprocessamento, com a Ásia-Pacífico liderando na fabricação e a Europa na demanda impulsionada por regulação. Os preços permanecerão com prêmio em relação às baterias de íons de lítio na maioria dos segmentos, justificado pela economia no descarte ao fim da vida útil e pelos benefícios de segurança. O mercado segue vulnerável à volatilidade dos preços das matérias-primas e à falta de padrões de desempenho unificados, o que pode atrasar ciclos de qualificação e retardar a adoção em setores regulados. Vetores e restrições da demanda Principais vetores de demanda - Metas corporativas de ESG e de pegada de carbono impulsionando a compra de soluções de armazenamento sustentáveis - Regulamentações ambientais rigorosas sobre descarte de baterias e materiais perigosos (por exemplo, REACH e restrições a PFAS) - Demanda por aplicações críticas de segurança, nas quais os riscos de fuga térmica das baterias convencionais são proibitivos - Crescimento das redes de IoT e do monitoramento ambiental, que exigem baterias de baixa potência, longa duração, descartáveis ou biodegradáveis - Avanços em bioprocessamento e química verde reduzindo custos de produção e melhorando o desempenho dos materiais - Aumento dos custos de descarte ao fim da vida útil das baterias convencionais, criando incentivo econômico para alternativas biodegradáveis Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - Densidade energética e potência menores em comparação com as baterias de íons de lítio, limitando o uso em aplicações de alto desempenho - Ausência de padrões unificados de desempenho e segurança específicos para químicas de base biológica, aumentando as exigências de qualificação - Qualidade e oferta inconsistentes de bio-precursores de alta pureza, gerando gargalos de produção - Custos iniciais mais altos em relação às tecnologias incumbentes, apesar da economia no descarte no longo prazo - Disponibilidade limitada de sistemas de gerenciamento de bateria sob medida e de equipamentos de conversão de energia adaptados às células de base

Partilhar Duas metodologias, centradas na Reflorestação e na Gestão Florestal Melhorada, foram lançadas pelo executivo. Mais projetos podem surgir, permitindo a redução de emissões carbónicas. O Mercado Voluntário de Carbono (MVC) passa a contar com três metodologias, em Portugal. O objetivo passa por reduzir as emissões carbónicas para a atmosfera, por forma a gerar créditos de carbono. Por decisão do Ministério do Ambiente e Energia, foram aprovadas duas novas metodologias de carbono dedicadas à Reflorestação e à Gestão Florestal Melhorada, que se juntam à já existente metodologia para Novas Florestações. A medida foi transmitida num comunicado enviado às redações. Na mira está o aumento das oportunidades para desenvolvimento de projetos de sequestro de carbono em território nacional e para a captação de investimento privado. Em causa está a geração de um crédito por cada tonelada de CO2 poupada em emissões. Posteriormente, os créditos podem ser vendidos a empresas que queiram libertar carbono para a atmosfera. “Estamos a criar condições para que mais proprietários, entidades e empresas possam investir na floresta e na ação climática", salienta a ministra do Ambiente e da Energia, Maria da Graça Carvalho. O alargamento das metodologias disponíveis permite reforçar "a credibilidade e a capacidade de crescimento do MVC", assim como incentivar ao "financiamento privado para projetos que contribuem simultaneamente para a neutralidade carbónica, valorização do território e resiliência das nossas florestas”, aponta. O MVC conta, à data, com dois projetos registados na metodologia Novas Florestações e um terceiro que aguarda validação inicial. Estão disponíveis para venda 977 créditos de carbono. Para tal, o Portal do Mercado Voluntário de Carbono conta com 29 utilizadores registados, ao mesmo tempo que existem 10 verificadores qualificados para assegurar a validação inicial e a verificação periódica dos projetos, informa o Ministério.

artigo.texto: Tesla’s Q3 Deliveries Beat UBS’ Estimates — But Energy Storage Miss Keeps This Analyst Neutral - The automaker delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3, about 5% above UBS’ consensus, according to investing.com. - Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh of energy-storage products, up from 13.5 GWh in Q2 and 12.5 GWh a year earlier - The brokerage said buyside expectations had been rising ahead of the deliveries report. Tesla (TSLA) remained on investors’ radar on Monday after better-than-expected third-quarter deliveries last Friday, though UBS said the beat was partially offset by weaker energy storage deployments. At the time of writing, TSLA shares were up 2%. UBS Sees Sustained Rebound In Vehicle Deliveries Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter (Q3), about 5% above UBS’ consensus, according to investing.com. Model 3 and Model Y accounted for 478,237 of those deliveries. The EV maker also produced 464,391 vehicles during the quarter, including 457,387 Model 3 and Model Y units. Deliveries rose about 1.3% from the previous quarter, while production increased nearly 3%. However, deliveries were still about 2% below the same period last year, when Tesla posted its highest-ever quarterly deliveries. UBS said buyside expectations had been rising ahead of the deliveries report and noted that the latest numbers showed a continued rebound in vehicle deliveries. Energy Storage Comes In Below Expectations Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh of energy-storage products, up from 13.5 GWh in the second quarter (Q2) and 12.5 GWh a year earlier. Still, the figure came in below expectations. UBS said the energy business can be difficult to forecast because deployment timing is often uneven. Since the segment carries above-average gross margins, the shortfall is expected to have a small impact on its model, worth roughly $0.03, UBS said. The firm reiterated a ‘Neutral’ rating on Tesla with a $385 price target, implying around 1.7% upside from current levels. Analysts Still Split On The Bigger Picture Earlier, Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster said the delivery data suggested the “EV winter” may be thawing, but Ross Gerber, CEO and co-founder of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth and Investment Management, was more cautious, noting that Tesla’s current annualized delivery pace remains below 2 million vehicles. JPMorgan also said Q3 sales were better than expected, helped by markets outside the U.S. and China, including stronger trends in Europe. However, the firm kept its below-consensus estimates due to expectations for lower automotive gross margins and higher spending. It also maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating and kept its $415 price target unchanged. Retail’s Take On TSLA Retail sentiment surrounding TSLA on Stocktwits remained in the ‘bullish’ zone over the past 24 hours. One user expects the stock to run up to $420 ahead of its Q3 earnings on October 21. Another user expects the stock to climb to $384 by the next session if it breaks the $378.56 resistance. Despite the recent recovery, TSLA is down 13% so far in 2026 and is the only stock in the Magnificent 7 cohort trading in the red. artigo.texto: Amphenol Advanced Sensors NTC thermistors & comprehensive sensor solutions According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Lithium Battery Thermal Runaway Sensor Modules market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global market for Lithium Battery Thermal Runaway Sensor Modules is entering a phase of structural expansion, with demand projected to accelerate steadily through 2035. These electronic modules and sensor systems detect early signs of thermal runaway in lithium-ion batteries, providing critical safety alerts for energy storage systems, electric vehicles, and consumer electronics. As battery deployments scale across grid-scale BESS, electric vehicles, and industrial applications, thermal runaway detection has shifted from a technical feature to a non-negotiable component for bankable projects. Insurance providers, project financiers, and regulators increasingly require certified detection layers, directly influencing project approval and financing terms. The market is bifurcating between cost-optimized modules for mass-market EVs and ruggedized multi-sensor systems for grid-scale storage, where failure costs are catastrophic. Supply chain constraints center on specialized sensor elements and application-specific integrated circuits, favoring vertically integrated specialists. System integration complexity, firmware algorithms, and seamless communication with battery management systems define competitive differentiation. Procurement is governed by stringent safety certifications such as UL 9540A and IEC 62619, creating high switching costs and locking in qualified suppliers. The competitive landscape is fragmenting into BMS manufacturers expanding into safety, industrial gas detection diversifiers, and specialized electronics contract manufacturers. Pricing is evolving toward value-based models encompassing cost-per-detection-point, integration software licenses, and long-term calibration services. Geographic deployment logic is decoupling from manufacturing hubs, with urgent demand in high-growth BESS and EV markets. The long-term outlook positions sensor modules as predictive health monitoring nodes, increasing their embedded value within battery assets. The baseline scenario for the Lithium Battery Thermal Runaway Sensor Modules market through 2035 anticipates sustained double-digit growth, underpinned by mandatory safety requirements in grid-scale energy storage and accelerating EV adoption. As battery energy storage systems become critical infrastructure, regulators and insurers are enforcing stringent thermal runaway detection standards, making sensor modules a prerequisite for project bankability. The market is expected to expand at a compound annual growth rate of 14.2% from 2026 to 2035, with the market index reaching 320 by 2035 (2025=100). This growth is not merely volume-driven; it reflects a shift toward higher-value, multi-parameter detection systems that integrate advanced algorithms to reduce false alarms and accelerate response times. Demand is bifurcating: mass-market EVs favor cost-optimized modules, while grid-scale BESS and premium EVs require ruggedized, multi-sensor systems with redundancy. Supply chain bottlenecks in specialized sensor elements and ASICs will favor vertically integrated suppliers and deep partnerships. System integration complexity remains a barrier, as modules must communicate seamlessly with BMS and energy management systems. Pricing is transitioning from per-unit hardware cost to value-based models, including cost-per-detection-point and software licenses, improving supplier margins and stickiness. Regionally, Asia-Pacific will lead in both production and demand, while North America and Europe drive regulatory hardening. The baseline assumes no major technological disruptions but anticipates gradual adoption of predictive health monitoring capabilities, further embedding sensor modules in battery lifecycle management. The electric vehicle sector represents the largest demand pool for lithium battery thermal runaway sensor modules, driven by the proliferation of EVs and increasingly stringent safety standards. Currently, EV manufacturers integrate sensor modules to detect early signs of thermal runaway, preventing catastrophic fires and ensuring passenger safety. As EV production scales globally, particularly in Asia-Pacific and Europe, demand for cost-effective yet reliable sensor modules will surge. Through 2035, the shift toward higher-energy-density batteries and faster charging will exacerbate thermal risks, necessitating more sophisticated multi-sensor systems. Demand-side indicators include EV production volumes, battery pack energy density, and regulatory safety mandates such as China's GB 38031 and Europe's UNECE R100. The mechanism is straightforward: as battery packs become more powerful, the potential severity of thermal runaway increases, making advanced detection indispensable. This will drive a transition from single-sensor to multi-parameter modules, with integrated algorithms to reduce false positives. Mass-market EVs will prioritize cost-optimized solutions, while premium and commercial vehicles will adopt ruggedized systems with redundancy. The sector's growth will be further supported by insurance and warranty requirements that mandate certified detection layers. artigo.texto: KP Group on Monday unveiled KP 3.0, a strategic roadmap that raises its FY32 targets to 10 GW of owned renewable generation through KPI Green Energy, 10 GW of third-party EPC execution, and 10 GWh of integrated battery manufacturing capacity, including cell production and BESS assembly. The announcement was made at the group’s Investor Day in Mumbai. The revised ambitions follow KP Group reaching a total portfolio of 9.21 GW across solar, wind, and hybrid assets, with the group saying the remaining capacity is expected to be added within the next few quarters. The group’s operating platform currently includes around 12,104 acres of land, 5.10 GW of power evacuation capacity, a 6.4 GW EPC portfolio, and a 2.8 GW IPP portfolio. KP 3.0 also introduces a new layer of professional leadership across renewable energy, international business, green hydrogen, investor relations, and governance. New business verticals being scaled include BESS through Sundrops Energia, floating solar with a 110 MW AC project at Kadana Dam in Gujarat, energy trading under CERC and GERC licences, and green hydrogen — with a 1 MW operational electrolysis plant at Matar producing 432 kg per day. The group is also pursuing international opportunities in Botswana, Zambia, Tanzania, and Saudi Arabia. In Botswana, an initial 500 MW phase is planned within a proposed 5 GW development. Founded in 1994, KP Group operates three publicly listed entities: KPI Green Energy, KP Energy, and KP Green Engineering. Published on October 5, 2026

Tesla (TSLA) remained on investors’ radar on Monday after better-than-expected third-quarter deliveries last Friday, though UBS said the beat was partially offset by weaker energy storage deployments. At the time of writing, TSLA shares were up 2%. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter (Q3), about 5% above UBS’ consensus, according to investing.com. Model 3 and Model Y accounted for 478,237 of those deliveries. The EV maker also produced 464,391 vehicles during the quarter, including 457,387 Model 3 and Model Y units. Deliveries rose about 1.3% from the previous quarter, while production increased nearly 3%. However, deliveries were still about 2% below the same period last year, when Tesla posted its highest-ever quarterly deliveries. UBS said buyside expectations had been rising ahead of the deliveries report and noted that the latest numbers showed a continued rebound in vehicle deliveries. Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh of energy-storage products, up from 13.5 GWh in the second quarter (Q2) and 12.5 GWh a year earlier. Still, the figure came in below expectations. UBS said the energy business can be difficult to forecast because deployment timing is often uneven. Since the segment carries above-average gross margins, the shortfall is expected to have a small impact on its model, worth roughly $0.03, UBS said. The firm reiterated a ‘Neutral’ rating on Tesla with a $385 price target, implying around 1.7% upside from current levels. Earlier, Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster said the delivery data suggested the “EV winter” may be thawing, but Ross Gerber, CEO and co-founder of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth and Investment Management, was more cautious, noting that Tesla’s current annualized delivery pace remains below 2 million vehicles. JPMorgan also said Q3 sales were better than expected, helped by markets outside the U.S. and China, including stronger trends in Europe. However, the firm kept its below-consensus estimates due to expectations for lower automotive gross margins and higher spending. It also maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating and kept its $415 price target unchanged. Retail sentiment surrounding TSLA on Stocktwits remained in the ‘bullish’ zone over the past 24 hours. One user expects the stock to run up to $420 ahead of its Q3 earnings on October 21. Another user expects the stock to climb to $384 by the next session if it breaks the $378.56 resistance. Despite the recent recovery, TSLA is down 13% so far in 2026 and is the only stock in the Magnificent 7 cohort trading in the red. artigo.texto: Do ronco ao silêncio: qual a diferença entre dirigir um carro elétrico e um a combustão? César Urnhani, piloto e especialista automotivo, mostra quais são essas diferenças e dá dicas para quem está fazendo essa transição. Crédito: Estadão Um vídeo viral acendeu o debate sobre a segurança e a resistência da infraestrutura de recarga de carros elétricos. No conteúdo que ganhou tração nas redes sociais chinesas, duas crianças aparecem brincando e usando os cabos de refrigeração líquida de uma estação Flash Charging da BYD como se fossem balanços. A tecnologia é a mesma que estreou no Brasil recentemente, com a inauguração do primeiro ponto de recarga ultrarrápida em Brasília (DF). O registro foi feito na cidade de Nanning, no sul da China. Nas imagens, as crianças aparecem segurando o conector e se balançando. Diante da repercussão, a BYD reforçou que é estritamente proibido brincar nos equipamentos e se comprometeu a intensificar a fiscalização e a manutenção física em suas estações. Como funciona o cabo suspenso do BYD Flash Charger O terminal de alta potência da BYD opera com arquitetura de 1.000V e utiliza um conector pesado (de 3 kg a 5 kg) instalado em um trilho suspenso. Esse sistema mantém o conector posicionado na altura do peito de um adulto, evitando que os cabos pesados com refrigeração líquida fiquem arrastando no chão sujo ou molhado. Saiba também: - Como saber quando um veículo carrega material radioativo? - Tem criança no carro? As dicas de segurança que salvam a vida do seu filho Contudo, o mecanismo suspenso não foi projetado para suportar forças dinâmicas ou o peso de uma pessoa se balançando. Risco mecânico é maior que o elétrico Embora as cenas gerem um receio imediato de eletrocussão, o risco elétrico é controlado por travas de segurança. Reportagem do Car News China lembra que, pelas normas técnicas, o sistema permanece totalmente desenergizado enquanto a pistola está encaixada no suporte. A corrente de alta voltagem só é liberada após o conector ser fisicamente acoplado ao veículo e passar por todas as verificações eletrônicas de comunicação. O maior perigo no incidente é mecânico e estrutural. O primeiro deles é de queda, com o desprendimento do cabo ou a perda de aderência pode causar a queda da criança e o impacto direto do pesado. Há também a possibilidade de danos internos. Diferentemente dos cabos comuns, a fiação resfriada a líquido possui uma estrutura interna complexa com canais de fluido refrigerante, linhas de comunicação e condutores de cobre. O movimento de balanço gera estresse e pode romper ou deformar esses componentes sem deixar marcas externas visíveis na capa de proteção. Essa degradação oculta representa um risco grave para o próximo cliente que for utilizar a estação, já que o cabo danificado será submetido a altíssimas correntes elétricas durante uma recarga rápida. Expansão da rede e novos desafios de infraestrutura A situação provocou discussões sobre a necessidade de atualizar os padrões de testes de engenharia desses equipamentos. Atualmente, os testes laboratoriais simulam esmagamento por pneus e tração linear, mas não consideram o estresse cíclico decorrente do mau uso em espaços públicos abertos. O desafio de reforçar a segurança física aumenta diante do ritmo de expansão da tecnologia. A BYD já conta com mais de 10 mil estações Flash Charging em operação na China, com a meta de alcançar 20 mil postos, além de planejar a ampliação da rede ultrarrápida para mercados internacionais, incluindo a América Latina e o Brasil. artigo.texto: Mount Pleasant committee revisits data center issues as moratorium advances MOUNT PLEASANT, S.C. (WCIV) — The Mount Pleasant Planning Committee plans to take another look at data center development at a Monday meeting, after steps were taken toward enacting a pause on new data center projects. According to the committee, Monday night's meeting will look at zoning rules and land use as the town continues to push toward a 120 day pause on new proposed data center projects. If the council approves the moratorium, leaders would be allowed more time to define what qualifies as a data center and create a public review process so that residents can have input on data center projects. There are reportedly no current large-scale data center proposals, however this meeting and the 120 day pause aims to help the committee put rules in place to help guide future projects before they are proposed. The committee will meet at 1:15 p.m. on Oct. 5.

artigo.texto: Energy-storage technology and manufacturing company Cygni Energy and telecom tower firm Indus Towers have decided to explore collaboration on sourcing energy storage solutions for telecom infrastructure in the country. The collaboration will include plans to establish Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing capacity of up to 1.5 GWh to address the evolving energy requirements of telecom infrastructure, Cygni Energy said on Monday following the signing of an MoU with Indus. The companies are also expected to evaluate advanced battery technologies for telecom applications, aimed at enhancing reliability, improving energy efficiency and enabling more sustainable telecom operations, the IIT Madras-incubated startup said. “For us, it is about building scale, technology capabilities and manufacturing readiness required to support the evolving energy needs of one of the world’s largest passive telecom infrastructure companies. We plan to develop capacity of up to 2 GWh, while building a portfolio that can evolve from today’s 100Ah solutions to higher-capacity 314Ah systems and emerging battery technologies,” founder and CEO Venkat Rajaraman said. Chairman of ITEL Foundation and Institute Professor, IIT Madras Ashok Jhunjhunwala said “collaboration between users, startups, manufacturers and technology institutions can support development and adoption of energy storage solutions in India. Telecom provides an important application for advancing battery technologies and manufacturing capabilities in this space.” Cygni opened a 4.8 GWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Gigafactory at E-Mobility Valley in the Electronics Manufacturing Cluster, Maheshwaram near Hyderabad in April 2025. Responding to queries, Mr. Rajaraman said the additional 1.5 GWh of capacity, being considered as part of the collaboration with Indus, is over and above the 4.8 GWh announced at inauguration. “We are currently expanding the Hyderabad facility to meet the Indus Towers requirement. The original 4.8 GWh capacity is intended to serve the utility-scale BESS segment,” he said. On how much the Hyderabad gigafactory is currently producing, he said “production varies month to month in line with customer demand and delivery schedules. Average capacity utilisation is approximately 50%, excluding the Indus Towers requirement, with production approaching full capacity in some months.” Published - October 05, 2026 08:14 pm IST This is a premium article, available exclusively to subscribers. artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no CEO da Nokia afirma que data centers seriam construídos “duas vezes mais rápido” sem restrições de fornecimento Publicado 05/10/2026 • 20:19 | Atualizado há 11 horas Ações brasileiras disparam com Bolsonaro agora visto como grande favorito para vencer a presidência Nasdaq bate novo recorde com alta das ações de tecnologia, apesar da pressão dos Treasuries Chefe da Saudi Aramco diz que recomposição dos estoques globais de petróleo pode levar dois anos Executivos da Anthropic, OpenAI, Google e Meta devem depor em audiência do Conselho Municipal de Nova York sobre os riscos da IA KEY POINTS Vesa Moilanen/Lehtikuva O CEO da Nokia afirmou que a indústria de tecnologia poderia construir data centers duas vezes mais rápido se não estivesse enfrentando as atuais restrições de fornecimento. Em entrevista à CNBC, ele destacou que a demanda por inteligência artificial continua forte, mesmo enquanto executivos das principais empresas do setor discutem a possibilidade de desacelerar o ritmo de desenvolvimento da tecnologia. “Não acho que se possa dizer, de forma alguma, que estamos construindo em excesso atualmente, porque a realidade é que, se pudéssemos construir duas vezes mais rápido, nossos clientes provavelmente também construiriam duas vezes mais rápido”, disse Justin Hotard ao podcast “The Tech Download”, da CNBC. “Isso me dá confiança de que ainda estamos nos estágios iniciais” da implementação da IA, acrescentou Hotard. A escassez de chips de memória essenciais e de energia está entre as principais restrições de fornecimento enfrentadas pelo setor. A Nokia, uma das maiores fabricantes de equipamentos de telecomunicações do mundo, reposicionou-se para se tornar uma empresa importante no segmento de infraestrutura para inteligência artificial. A companhia fornece a tecnologia necessária para conectar racks de chips dentro dos data centers, além de soluções que interligam data centers localizados em diferentes regiões. Leia mais: Nokia amplia parceria com Microsoft para acelerar automação de redes com inteligência artificial O papel cada vez mais relevante da Nokia como uma empresa que “fornece ferramentas e recursos práticos” para o boom da IA parece ter conquistado os investidores. As ações da companhia acumulam alta de cerca de 130% no último ano. Ainda assim, permanece o debate sobre se a indústria está construindo data centers em um ritmo excessivamente acelerado e se haverá demanda suficiente para sustentar toda essa infraestrutura. Os investimentos na expansão da inteligência artificial — incluindo data centers, chips e infraestrutura relacionada — devem totalizar US$ 10,3 trilhões (cerca de R$ 56,2 trilhões) entre 2025 e 2032, o equivalente a uma média de 3,63% do Produto Interno Bruto dos Estados Unidos por ano, de acordo com uma pesquisa apresentada no Brookings Papers on Economic Activity. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC As empresas estão recorrendo a dívidas, joint ventures e outros mecanismos complexos de financiamento para levantar recursos destinados a esses projetos, que dependem da manutenção de uma demanda elevada por serviços de IA no longo prazo. As preocupações em relação ao ritmo de desenvolvimento da IA também aumentaram diante de alertas sobre os riscos de segurança da tecnologia. Entre eles estão as advertências de um pesquisador da Anthropic sobre uma possível ameaça existencial, que levaram o CEO da empresa, Dario Amodei, a defender uma desaceleração no desenvolvimento dos modelos mais avançados. Leia mais: Nokia diz que I.A e computação em nuvem impulsionaram vendas no segundo trimestre A declaração provocou uma onda de vendas de ações ligadas à inteligência artificial no mês passado. Hotard, no entanto, afirmou que a demanda por IA não depende apenas do lançamento de novos modelos por empresas de ponta como Anthropic e OpenAI. “Acho que a realidade é que, mesmo estando onde estamos hoje, ainda estamos no início da implementação, e o poder desses modelos é tão grande que existe muita demanda a ser atendida apenas na fase de implementação”, disse Hotard. “Mesmo que não tivéssemos outro modelo de ponta lançado nos próximos três anos, provavelmente poderíamos fazer avanços enormes apenas implementando a tecnologia que já existe hoje.” 🔷 Canal 562 ClaroTV+ | Canal 562 Sky | Canal 592 Vivo | Canal 187 Oi | Operadoras regionais 🔷 TV SINAL ABERTO: parabólicas canal 562 🔷 ONLINE: www.timesbrasil.com.br | YouTube 🔷 FAST Channels: Samsung TV Plus, LG Channels, TCL Channels, Pluto TV, Roku, Zapping | Novos Streamings Este conteúdo foi fornecido pela CNBC Internacional e a responsabilidade exclusiva pela tradução para o português é do Times Brasil.

artigo.texto: Adaptogen Capital, a specialist investment firm at the forefront of the energy transition, is pleased to announce the next phase of its European growth strategy, as it targets €1bn of investment opportunities by 2030 across European Battery Energy Storage (BESS) markets. Highlights: - Adaptogen has developed a 1.2GW pipeline of Belgian BESS opportunities, with five initial projects in development and progressing towards final investment decision (FID). - Adaptogen has also progressed a further 500MW portfolio in Germany across two sites at key offshore wind HV landing points on the transmission grid. - Adaptogen’s first fund, closed in 2023, has now been fully committed to the development and operation of UK BESS assets through its operating platform Varco Energy, with a follow on co-investment raise in 2025. - Adaptogen is now exploring capital raising in 2027 to assist in funding its initial European BESS assets, with a likely requirement of €260m equity and €500m of debt. Adaptogen Capital today sets out its continued expansion into continental Europe, having built a pipeline of Belgian opportunities through its operating platform MVA Energy, that address grid congestion and the integration of growing renewable generation, alongside a parallel German pipeline. The firm’s approach is structured around project-specific capital commitments at FID, allowing infrastructure investors the opportunity to back firm connection projects with low grid fees once development and permitting risk has been substantially reduced. Investor appetite for European battery energy storage is strengthening as power market volatility, geopolitical and inflation concerns, rising renewable penetration and growing grid constraints reinforce the role of storage as critical energy infrastructure. With relatively few specialist BESS managers operating at scale across the region, Adaptogen believes its project-led approach is well aligned with the needs of infrastructure investors seeking exposure to the central asset class in the next phase of the energy transition. Adaptogen’s European ambitions build directly on its UK experience. The firm’s original fund closed in 2023 and has since been fully deployed to develop, construct and operate grid-scale BESS assets through its Varco Energy platform, with 350MW on track to be operational by 2028 and a further 275MW in development. Battery energy storage is increasingly recognised across Europe as critical infrastructure for balancing intermittent renewable generation and easing grid congestion. Adaptogen’s disciplined, project-led approach to capital deployment is intended to support that transition as it extends its strategy beyond the UK. James Mills, Managing Director, Adaptogen Capital, commented: “Across Europe, grids are under growing pressure from the pace of renewable build-out, and that is creating a clear investment case for well-located, grid scale battery storage with firm connections, backed by sensibly structured revenue and debt facilities. We have spent the past three years building a pipeline that targets that opportunity, and our approach of committing capital once projects have reached final investment decision allows infrastructure investors to back assets where development risk has already been substantially reduced. Our experience delivering and operating storage assets in the UK through Varco Energy gives us a strong foundation as we extend that model into continental Europe.” Building, Design & Construction Magazine | The Choice of Industry Professionals

artigo.texto: BYD's Xixian Battery Plant Hits Full Throttle as Washington Delays Connected-Vehicle Ban Published on 10/04/2026 at 13:51 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD's newest battery cell facility in Xixian, Shaanxi province, has reached full production, the company's Yicai-reported milestone arriving just as its shares came under pressure from a global bond-market selloff. The plant, built at a cost of 7 billion CNY, carries an annual capacity of 16 gigawatt-hours and ranks among the first sites manufacturing BYD's second-generation Blade battery. Bringing cell production in-house is central to the automaker's strategy of keeping manufacturing costs in check. That operational progress, announced Wednesday, stood in contrast to the stock's performance. BYD shares finished Friday at 8.39 EUR on European trading venues, down 2.4% on the day, as surging US Treasury yields triggered a broad retreat across Asian equity markets. Several Chinese electric-vehicle makers, Li Auto and XPeng among them, fell in sympathy, though Geely managed to buck the trend. JPMorgan Cuts Its Rating Market sentiment was further dented by JPMorgan, which downgraded BYD from Overweight to Neutral and slashed its price target to 88 HKD from 124 HKD. The brokerage pointed to lackluster domestic demand, rising input costs, and persistent trade-policy and regulatory uncertainty facing Chinese carmakers. The downgrade was reported Wednesday, with some accounts placing the move a day earlier. The cautious stance reflects a home market where consumers remain on the sidelines. According to Reuters, BYD continues to grapple with weak demand in China, where a bruising price war has made buyers hesitant. Investors in Hong Kong responded tepidly to the company's latest disclosures, with the local listing slipping after trading resumed Friday. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Exports Do the Heavy Lifting September delivery figures, released Thursday, laid bare the split between home and abroad. Total vehicle sales climbed 17% year over year to 463,561 units, but the expansion was powered overwhelmingly by overseas markets: exports of passenger cars and pickups outside China jumped 153.9% to 179,877 units. Those booming shipments are doing much of the work of offsetting the sluggish domestic picture. The overseas push, however, cuts both ways. It opens fresh sales channels while drawing Chinese manufacturers deeper into the crosshairs of foreign regulators and trade officials. A Reprieve in Washington On that front, the US Senate on Wednesday postponed deliberations on a bill that would permanently bar the import, production, and sale of connected vehicles and related hardware and software with Chinese links. The delay hands Chinese automakers, BYD included, a temporary breather from looming restrictions on access to the North American market. For the year to date, unaudited company figures show total sales of 3,131,576 vehicles across the first nine months, a decline of 3.94% compared with the same period a year earlier. After the recent losses, the stock trades 4.5% above its 52-week low. The picture for investors is one of a company pulled in two directions: an overseas expansion that is generating real momentum, set against trade-policy decisions in Washington and elsewhere that remain a significant wildcard for the business ahead. artigo.texto: Nvidia e Broadcom se isolam de impacto de crise de energia em data centers dos EUA, diz Morgan Stanley 5 Out (Reuters) - Nvidia e Broadcom estão relativamente protegidas contra o agravamento da crise de energia nas centrais de processamento de dados dos Estados Unidos, afirmou o Morgan Stanley em relatório nesta segunda-feira. Porém, qualquer atraso resultante nas implantações de infraestrutura para inteligência artificial pode afetar os fabricantes de chips de memória, componentes ópticos e outros processadores secundários. O banco estimou no mês passado que os desenvolvedores de data centers nos EUA enfrentarão um déficit líquido de energia de 34% até 2028, equivalente a 32 GW. O boom da IA gerou bilhões de dólares em investimentos em data centers, mas as enormes necessidades de computação e eletricidade da IA generativa estão cada vez mais esbarrando nos problemas de fornecimento de eletricidade nos EUA. Tanto Morgan Stanley quanto Goldman Sachs sinalizaram restrições crescentes à expansão dos data centers nos EUA; o GS espera um impacto limitado no curto prazo devido à resistência política, enquanto o MS vê desafios relacionados à mão de obra, energia e política. O Morgan Stanley afirmou que não vê os gargalos colocando em risco as previsões da Nvidia ou da Broadcom para 2027, citando a visibilidade dessas empresas quanto à alocação de chips, à expansão geográfica e à coordenação entre centros de dados, fornecedores de chips e a cadeia de abastecimento de energia. Se a capacidade de produção de chips não puder ser implantada, os clientes poderão adiar entregas ou cancelar pedidos, sendo que componentes de memória, óptica, gerenciamento de energia e analógicos são os mais expostos a problemas de fornecimento, afirmou o Morgan Stanley. artigo.texto: Discussão na Cúpula: Solera, BYD e CITS Traçam o Futuro da Indústria NEV da China AGÊNCIA DE COMUNICAÇÃO Conteúdo de responsabilidade da empresa 5 de outubro de 2026 SHENZHEN, China, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — A Solera Holdings, LLC. (“Solera”), uma líder global em gestão do ciclo de vida de veículos e soluções digitais de segurança no transporte, recentemente fez uma visita de alto nível à sede global da BYD. A Sra. Jing Liao, Diretora Administrativa da Solera e Presidente da Solera Foundation, liderou a delegação da Solera em discussões com o Sr. Lian Yubo, Diretor de Tecnologia e Cientista Chefe da BYD, Engenheiro Automotivo Chefe, Presidente do Automotive Engineering Research Institute e Acadêmico da Chinese Academy of Engineering, juntamente com sua equipe de gestão. A Sra. Yang Ying, Vice-Presidente e Secretária Geral da China Intelligent Transportation Systems Association (CITS), e o Sr. Wang Junming, Vice-Presidente da CITS, também participaram da reunião. A relação entre a BYD e a Solera começou há anos e vem se fortalecendo desde então mercado a mercado, desafio a desafio passando a ser a parceria ampla e global que as duas empresas trazem para discussão hoje. Esse nível de profundidade e abrangência só é alcançado após anos de trabalho conjunto em diversos mercados em todo o mundo. Esta visita marca o próximo capítulo: um compromisso compartilhado com o avanço da segurança rodoviária e a construção da infraestrutura que irá apoiar a indústria NEV da China na sua expansão em todo o mundo. Os participantes realizaram discussões aprofundadas sobre a expansão global da indústria de novos veículos de energia (NEV) da China, o desenvolvimento de ecossistemas de serviços no exterior, a colaboração internacional da indústria e as oportunidades futuras de cooperação. O Sr. SooCheon Chung, Diretor Administrativo da Solera na Ásia, e o Sr. Jason Liu, Diretor de Vendas da Solera China, também participaram da reunião. Foto: A equipe de gestão da Solera visita a Sede Global da BYD e posa para uma foto em grupo com o Sr. Lian Yubo, Diretor de Tecnologia e Cientista Chefe da BYD, Engenheiro Automotivo Chefe, Presidente do Automotive Engineering Research Institute e Acadêmico da Chinese Academy of Engineering, sua equipe e líderes da CITS. Durante a reunião, foram realizadas discussões profundas sobre as oportunidades e os desafios enfrentados pelos fabricantes chineses de veículos de nova energia (NEV) na sua expansão para os mercados internacionais. As discussões se concentraram nos principais elementos do desenvolvimento do ecossistema pós-venda no exterior, incluindo gerenciamento do ciclo de vida do veículo, desenvolvimento da rede de serviços pós-venda, aprimoramento da capacidade de reparo, serviços de seguros e sinistros, desenvolvimento de ecossistemas de dados, e conformidade regulatória nos mercados globais. Na reunião também foram discutidos pontos de vista sobre o desenvolvimento de redes globais de serviços de pós-venda e a capacitação de talentos técnicos, abrangendo como informações de reparo, programas de treinamento técnico e ferramentas digitais podem apoiar a melhoria contínua das capacidades de reparo e da eficiência operacional nos mercados internacionais. Os representantes da Solera, CITS e BYD realizaram discussões sobre a expansão global da indústria NEV da China e o desenvolvimento de ecossistemas de pós-venda no exterior. Com a aceleração da expansão global da indústria NEV da China torna-se cada vez mais importante a construção de um ecossistema de serviços internacionais que dê suporte a todo o ciclo de vida do veículo. Durante as discussões, a equipe da BYD compartilhou insights da sua experiência com o crescimento internacional da empresa, incluindo perspectivas sobre o desenvolvimento da rede de serviços no exterior, recursos operacionais localizados e colaboração mais ampla do ecossistema da indústria. Os participantes também compartilharam pontos de vista sobre tópicos como acesso a informações de reparo e manutenção nos mercados internacionais, requisitos de conformidade de dados, e desenvolvimento de peças e ecossistemas de serviços. O Sr. Zhong Yilin, Vice-Presidente do Automotive Engineering Research Institute da BYD, comentou: “A expansão da indústria NEV da China em todo o mundo está tornando cada vez evidente a importância da construção de ecossistemas de serviços robustos. O fortalecimento adicional das redes de reparo e serviço no exterior, o desenvolvimento de talentos técnicos e o aprimoramento das capacidades de serviço adaptadas às necessidades do mercado local são prioridades vitais para as marcas automotivas chinesas que buscam o crescimento internacional.” A Sra. Yang Ying, Vice-Presidente e Secretária Geral da China Intelligent Transportation Systems Association (CITS), endossou essa visão e acrescentou: O apoio ao desenvolvimento internacional das empresas chinesas NEV continua a ser uma área de foco essencial para a CITS. Continuaremos a fazer o nosso papel como plataforma de colaboração e intercâmbio internacional para ajudar as empresas automotivas chinesas a expandir sua atuação para mercados externos e a alcançar um crescimento sustentável de longo prazo.” Os participantes concordaram que uma colaboração mais estreita em toda a cadeia de valor automotiva e melhorias contínuas na capacidade global de suporte de serviços fornecerão uma base sólida para a expansão da presença internacional das marcas automotivas chinesas. Para a BYD e as seguradoras que apoiam seu crescimento internacional, a relevância da Solera é direta: sua infraestrutura foi desenvolvida especificamente para veículos elétricos e de nova energia, e não adaptada de sistemas da era da combustão. Isso inclui a inteligência de risco relacionada a veículos elétricos e baterias, que oferece às seguradoras uma visão clara dos custos de reparos, riscos de sinistros e condições da bateria; dados de sinistros e reparos com base em IA, com credibilidade nos principais mercado

artigo.texto: Colleton County settles lawsuit, creating exclusion zone for data centers in ACE Basin WALTERBORO, SC (WCIV) — Colleton County has reached a settlement with the Southern Environmental Law Center that will prohibit data center development across much of the ACE Basin, ending a legal challenge over a county ordinance that opened rural areas to large-scale data center projects. The agreement resolves a lawsuit filed in January by Colleton County residents Miles Crosby and Jennifer Singleton, who challenged county zoning changes that allowed data centers in rural portions of the county through a special-exception process. Under the settlement, Colleton County will establish a "Data Center Exclusion Area" as part of its Comprehensive Plan, identifying areas deemed unsuitable for data center development. "This historic settlement agreement sets the framework for legislative action that will ensure responsible conservation of natural resources while securing the economic future for citizens of Colleton County," Colleton County Council Chairman Scott Biering said in a statement. The agreement follows months of intense public debate surrounding a proposed Eagle Rock Partners data center campus south of Walterboro. The project, first unveiled in late 2025, called for an approximately 859-acre, 1,000-megawatt development near the headwaters of the Ashepoo River in the ACE Basin, prompting strong opposition from residents concerned about impacts to the environment, water resources and the region's rural character. READ MORE | Colleton County residents raise concerns over proposed data center, power plant projects According to the Southern Environmental Law Center, the exclusion area will cover most of the ACE Basin within Colleton County, including ecologically sensitive lands along the Ashepoo, Combahee and Edisto rivers. The exclusion area also includes the roughly 850-acre tract where the original Eagle Rock proposal was planned. "The original data center complex that was proposed would have surrounded my property on three sides and completely changed the area," Miles Crosby said in a statement released by SELC. "I'm thankful we could reach an outcome that not only prevents data centers from surrounding my home but also protects the majority of the ACE Basin in Colleton County from data center development." Jennifer Singleton, another plaintiff in the case, called the settlement a compromise that protects one of South Carolina's most significant natural resources. "It's been a long and winding road to get here, but I'm thrilled we were able to reach a compromise that establishes a 'Data Center Exclusion Area' in Colleton County," Singleton said. "The ACE Basin is a treasure we must all work together to care for." County Administrator Thomas Higgs said the settlement demonstrates that economic development and environmental protection can coexist as South Carolina continues to attract new investment. "We understand South Carolina currently faces many economic development issues. Data centers are a current national security topic and developers have their eyes on South Carolina," Higgs said. "In every economic development scenario, the challenge is to protect South Carolina itself, and moreover, its natural resources." The ACE Basin encompasses roughly 1.6 million acres across the Ashepoo, Combahee and Edisto river systems and has long been recognized as one of the nation's most significant conservation landscapes. More than 300,000 acres have been permanently protected since the formation of the ACE Basin Task Force in 1989, according to SELC. SELC South Carolina Director Chris DeScherer called the settlement "a significant victory for the ACE Basin" and said the organization looks forward to working with county leaders to ensure future data center projects are developed responsibly. County officials said they hope the agreement can serve as a model for other South Carolina communities seeking to balance economic growth with conservation.

artigo.texto: [ESPAÑOL ABAJO | PORTUGUÊS ABAIXO] Colombia’s new government will initiate proceedings to lift a 50% cap on carbon credit retirements against CO2 tax liabilities – handing a win to voluntary carbon market (VCM) sellers, and boosting the significance of compliance measures in response to trade pressures from the EU. Minister of Environment and Sustainable Development Fabio Arjona announced in Medellin that the new government of right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella would propose the change to Congress. Latin American and Caribbean countries enjoy relatively low trade exposure to the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which prices in the embedded carbon of goods entering the bloc. Still, Colombia ranks just behind Brazil as the most EU CBAM-exposed Latin American or Caribbean countries. Colombia’s COP 29,070.49 ($8.76) per tonne CO2 tax rate may alleviate some of the border carbon burden by creating an EU-recognised domestic carbon price that’s deductible from CBAM fees. In its current form, the European Commission’s draft implementing act would make the price paid for carbon credits retired under the tax eligible for deductions, too – enhancing the role of the VCM to address both domestic and international carbon pricing compliance. Arjona simultaneously announced the revocation of Ministerial Decree 0973 on the VCM, which established restrictions in line with former President Gustavo Petro’s criticisms of the market and was published in early August. EMISSIONS TRADING SYSTEMS Both Colombia and Brazil are working to implement emissions trading systems – called the ‘PNCTE’ in Colombia, and the ‘SBCE’ in Brazil. These schemes could also create EU-recognised carbon prices. In Brazil, carbon project co-developer Earthshot Labs Brazil has seen some foreign investors take a cautious approach due to uncertainty in the SBCE’s final design, Carbon Pulse reported last week. That does not mean that investment in the Brazilian VCM has halted, according to the co-developer’s director Rita Croce – rather, some investors are holding out for projects that could potentially generate Article 6 Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs) in the future. Brazil’s increasingly crowded carbon asset ecosystem would include SBCE allowances, called CBEs; SBCE-eligible voluntary carbon credits, called CRVEs; voluntary credits bearing a Letter of Authorisation; and regular voluntary units. Purchasing either CBEs or CRVEs for use in the SBCE could potentially fall under the European Commission’s draft vision for a ‘carbon price effectively paid’ in a third country, for CBAM purposes. Meanwhile, Colombia’s Ministerial Decree 0969 from the now-departed Petro administration stated that up to 3.3% of PNCTE compliance units could be sourced from the VCM – a far lower percentage than what was initially pitched in a Sep. 2024 consultation document. The fate of the PNCTE under De La Espriella is unclear. J-REDD+ QUESTIONS Meanwhile, a Brazilian state and Argentine province grappled with thorny implementation questions for jurisdictional REDD+ (J-REDD+). A proposed road in the Amazon could result in up to 133,800 hectares of additional deforestation over 20 years – putting Brazilian state Acre’s J-REDD+ goals at risk, according to a report published by NGOs Amazon Conservation and SOS Amazonia. Acre’s J-REDD+ programme is registered under the ART standard’s TREES protocol. Researchers noted that the modelling is not meant to predict actual future losses, but that plans for new road developments placed Acre at “a critical juncture”. In Argentina, senators for the province of Misiones – itself promoting a large-scale, Verra-registered J-REDD+ programme – are mounting partial opposition to a national bill they helped draft. Senator Sonia Rojas Decut has taken issue with the bill’s definition of ‘project owner’ (Spanish: titular del proyecto). The definition would effectively require written consent from thousands of native forest owners to implement programmes at the provincial level, she argued. The bill would therefore “make it impossible for Argentine provinces to implement jurisdictional programmes”, she wrote. Argentine media has reported that while the bill disappeared from the agenda for last week’s Senate session, members of ruling party La Libertad Avanza have indicated that they will participate in ongoing negotiations with Misiones in hopes of bringing the bill to a future session. NEWS By Alejandra Padin-Dujon – [email protected] [ESPAÑOL] Cambio de postura colombiana sobre la compensación de emisiones podría abrir oportunidades comerciales con la UE El nuevo gobierno de Colombia iniciará los trámites para eliminar el límite del 50% a la cancelación de créditos de carbono para cubrir obligaciones del impuesto al CO2, una medida favorable para los vendedores del mercado voluntario de carbono (VCM), mientras las medidas de cumplimiento cobran mayor relevancia ante las presiones comerciales de la UE. El ministro de ambiente y desarrollo sostenible, Fabio Arjona, anunció en Medellín que el nuevo gobierno del presidente derechista Abelardo De La Espriella propondría el cambio al Congreso. artigo.texto: KALAMAZOO, MI (WKZO AM/FM) – It has been one of the least controversial issues the Kalamazoo city commission has had to deal with this year, but one of the most emotional. Opinions have been nearly unanimous that the city needs to brace itself, and thoroughly prepare for the day someone wants to build a data center, or any other potentially worrisome high-tech facility in town. They have scheduled a final public hearing and a vote this evening. Kalamazoo city commissioners are set to finalize a one year moratorium, to buy time to redraft zoning codes to make sure if a data center or large battery energy storage system is proposed, that it won’t become a problem for its neighbors or the community. Assistant City Planner Bobby Durkee says that one year clock begins with tonight’s approval. “The goal of the moratorium is to develop those zoning standards and appropriate land uses, and to study for a transparent public process. For staff in the community to research the topic, understand the topic and draft regulations because you cannot outright ban a use.” He says as recommended by the planning commission, staff will set up a working group to assist in the research. “You know I look at things like public utilities, private utilities, residents, neighborhoods, the industry itself.” Several commissioners implored him not to make it top-heavy with industry and utility experts and to make sure it represents community and environmental interests too. Commissioner Chris Praedel says it’s “so critically important that there are people sitting in those seats that are just everyday people, you know, that care a lot about this issue.” While communities have some flexibility in how it sets up its own zoning regulations, it’s still a process that is guided by state laws and technical requirements and must be detailed and specific if a community wants to avoid legal challenges, or leave gaps or loopholes. Data centers have become a major state and national issue this election year with national polls showing 65 to 70% of the public opposed to having a data center in their community and only 20% supporting. The numbers are even higher for Democratic and younger voters.

artigo.texto: COLDWATER, MI (WTVB) – Coldwater city officials are in the process of trying to make the community as unattractive as possible to potential developers of data centers. This comes after a joint session on August 19 involving Coldwater government boards. They heard a presentation that evening on data centers from Jean Hardy of Michigan State University whose research centers on the role of technology in rural economic and community development. City Planner Robert Hawley told the Coldwater Planning Commission on Monday night they and their consultants from McKenna and Associates are currently working on zoning ordinance amendments that would define data centers. Mayor Tom Kramer emphasized there was no desire among City Council members to bring a data center to Coldwater. But Kramer added that by law, they have to offer something to potential developers. A draft could be presented to the Planning Commission on November 16 with a public hearing possibly taking place in December. Hardy said in August that the backlash across the state from communities opposing data centers has now caused those companies to rethink the prospects of building new facilities in the state. In other business, the Planning Commission approved a new Master Plan and sent it on to the City Council for final approval. It was compiled after a year of community surveys, steering committee meetings, and focus groups. The Master Plan for Coldwater has not been updated since 2017. It outlines goals and infrastructure strategies to guide the future growth of Coldwater.

artigo.texto: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The deferment of the carbon tax implementation is aligned with the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry’s efforts to establish a complete regulatory and policy framework before enforcing emission caps. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the government decided to delay the tax, originally planned for this year, following global geopolitical developments that led to volatile energy prices, providing affected industries with a necessary buffer. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. That’s why we’ve been successful in launching the National Carbon Market Policy and I hope that we can table the Climate Change Act soon. “Once that is up, then we have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including the regulation, enforcement, the regulatory powers to give us to set the emission ceiling, and then we can know anything above the ceiling, then the carbon tax will come into place as a penalty to the polluters. “So, we’re not looking at this year for the carbon tax,” he said. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. He added that while operators need adequate time for feasibility studies and modifications, strict progress is required to qualify for temporary extensions. The session, titled “Building A Resilient Malaysia: Environment, Climate And Our Future”, was moderated by Bernama chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai. Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, as well as members of the local and foreign media based in Malaysia. Uploaded by Tham Yek Lee

artigo.texto: UAE-based real assets investor and developer ROX Capital Group has launched the ROX Gulf Energy Storage Platform, targeting utility-scale and commercial energy storage projects in the UAE and Oman while exploring opportunities for regional assembly and manufacturing. The platform will evaluate a range of storage technologies, including vanadium redox flow, lithium iron phosphate and sodium-ion batteries, as well as long-duration solutions such as CO₂ batteries, gravity-based storage, compressed-air energy storage and thermal storage. ROX plans to establish partnerships with selected technology providers based on their track record in deploying large-scale storage projects, long-duration storage expertise where applicable, financial and operational capacity, and ownership or control of core technology intellectual property. The company said it will prioritise providers with bankable systems, established manufacturing capabilities and the ability to offer long-term technical support, performance guarantees and warranties. The platform and its partners will pursue upcoming energy storage tenders and assess local assembly or manufacturing opportunities where commercially viable. “The Gulf is building some of the world’s largest solar projects. The next challenge is ensuring that clean power remains available after sunset and during periods of peak demand,” said Robin Antony, Founder of ROX Capital Group. “No single technology will meet every requirement. We are building a platform that matches the right technology to the needs of each project and, where viable, supports the development of local manufacturing capability.” “Lithium-ion batteries have transformed energy storage and will remain an important part of the solution,” Antony added. “However, the Gulf’s climate, load profile and energy-security priorities create a need for a broader portfolio of technologies. High summer temperatures can increase cooling requirements, while solar-heavy systems require storage over longer periods after dark. We see an important role for technologies including vanadium flow batteries, CO₂ batteries, gravity-based storage and thermal storage alongside lithium-ion solutions.” -TradeArabia News Service

artigo.texto: By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Oct. 5: Headway Earth and Rezonance, led by international carbon-market expert Dr. Divaldo Rezende, have launched the Carbon Market Development Mission Nepal to help develop the country’s emerging carbon-market and climate-finance ecosystem. The initiative aims to build Nepal’s capacity to develop climate projects, strengthen carbon-market infrastructure and connect Nepali projects with international climate finance, investors and carbon buyers. Nepal has significant potential in areas including forests, agriculture, renewable energy, waste management, biochar and other climate solutions. The mission seeks to turn this potential into bankable climate projects, investment, employment and sustainable development opportunities for Nepali communities and businesses, said Pratik Karki, Founder and Managing Director of Headway Earth. The mission will initially focus on three areas—capacity development, project development, and climate finance and market access. Under capacity development, the initiative will seek to strengthen knowledge, skills and institutional capacity among government agencies, financial institutions, businesses, communities and other stakeholders on carbon markets, climate finance and international climate policy, Karki added. Similarly, it will identify, design and develop high-quality climate and carbon projects across the country, with an emphasis on projects capable of attracting investment and delivering measurable environmental, social and economic benefits. The mission will also seek to connect Nepali projects with international investors, climate funds, financial institutions, development partners and carbon buyers, creating pathways for Nepali climate projects to access global markets. A key objective of the initiative is to help establish the institutional and financial infrastructure needed for a functioning national carbon ecosystem. Highlighting the opportunities in Nepal, Dr. Rezende said Nepal has an opportunity to strengthen international confidence and position itself as an attractive destination for climate investment. “The world wants to come to Nepal. Nepal is committing to zero corruption, and this can create a new level of confidence among international investors and climate partners,” he said. Dr. Rezende brings extensive international experience in carbon markets, climate finance and sustainable development. He will work alongside Headway Earth to support Nepal’s integration into global climate-finance and carbon-market opportunities. As part of its long-term vision, Headway Earth and Rezonance plan to work towards developing a Carbon Fund and Carbon Bank for Nepal to mobilise domestic and international capital for credible climate projects, said Prakash Gyawali, Chief Executive Officer of Headway Earth. The initiative also aims to support the development and integration of a national carbon registry and carbon marketplace to improve transparency, traceability and market access for Nepali carbon and climate assets. Technology and transparent measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) of climate impacts will form an important foundation of the proposed ecosystem. According to CEO Gyawali, the initiative is not limited to generating carbon credits but aims to establish the wider ecosystem required to support the carbon market, including projects, technology, finance, capacity, a registry, a marketplace and access to international markets.

artigo.texto: As if Emporia’s data center debate needed any more controversy. With the general election essentially a month away, Emporians for Progress spokesman Casey Woods says the ordinance language behind the petitions hoping to ban data centers and battery energy storage systems don’t reference city Planning and Zoning regulations currently on the books. The petitions reference Article 15, but Planning and Zoning code uses Sections instead of Articles and only goes up to Section 12. Emporia Neighbors United founder Jay Vehige sees things differently, although he admits there was a “drafting error” before the petition was turned in. The original petition and ordinance were submitted July 14, according to City Manager Trey Cocking. It was certified by the Lyon County Clerk’s Office on July 21 and was passed by the Emporia City Commission on August 5. Cocking says Vehige tried to submit revised petitions August 7, but he tells KVOE News cities have no ability to alter what was originally submitted — meaning residents have to vote on the original package due to KSA 12-3013. This is the second clerical or drafting error in this petition process for Emporia Neighbors United. The original petitions submitted were invalidated because petition circulators didn’t verify they witnessed petitions being signed. Vehige has told KVOE News that issue was due to a paperwork error in attaching circulator forms to signature petition forms. Woods says Emporians for Progress sees this as one reason to oppose the ballot questions. Vehige counters Woods’ assertions, saying his guidance indicates the Article 15 reference would not invalidate both petitions in their entirety. Vehige also says he has spoken with City Attorney Christina Montgomery, who was out of the office last week and is currently unavailable for an interview. Cocking sent a statement to KVOE News. saying the Article 15 reference will be one issue to be addressed by the court for effect and “enforceability.” He also says the city is not speculating how this will be addressed in court with that process a distinct possibility. Woods sees potential lawsuits throughout the 10-year halt if the questions are approved. The city has asked for rulings on whether the petitions are legislative or administrative in nature. Administrative rulings would likely invalidate the petitions — and, if the petitions are approved but Kansas Senior Judge Glenn Braun rules the petitions are administrative after the Nov. 3 general election, the vote results would be invalidated as well. Vehige believes Judge Braun will side with Emporia Neighbors United. There is no date for when Judge Braun will rule on the nature of the 2 ballot questions. This continues a busy time for news when it comes to data centers locally. A lawsuit filed by Emporia City Commissioner Erren Harter against Recall Committee members Haley Bradford, Kathleen Lamb and Vehige — also including Lyon County Legal Counsel Molly Priest and County Clerk Amie Jones as defendants — ended Thursday with an “agreed upon order” that essentially says this version of a recall petition cannot move forward under any circumstances. Priest and the case paperwork say this does not stop future petitions seeking Harter’s recall cannot move forward. A grand jury determining whether Harter conducted misconduct in office will be empaneled Monday. Meanwhile, Amanda Mendoza, Kenneth Bruner, Ann Bruner and the separate Bruner trusts have filed a lawsuit against the city of Emporia, alleging the zoning part of the Digital Infrastructure overlay was not properly handled. The lawsuit, LY-2026-CV-124, says the Emporia Planning Commission did not have either the jurisdiction or the authorization to review applications for zoning classifications that did not exist when applications were filed — meaning, according to the lawsuit, the city’s decision to approve the overlay was unlawful and the subsequent rezoning of 11 tracts of land was unauthorized and without proper jurisdiction. On top of that, Vehige says Emporia Neighbors United will push to bring 2 more petitions to the ballot by early next year. One would change the form of city government from its current at-large City Commission structure to a 4-ward City Council system with one at-large position. The other would change the method of filling unexpired City Commission or City Council positions from appointment to public vote. In separate news related to the Emporia data center project, the Flint Hills Digital Campus website is no longer public-facing. The website went public in early June as the data center project was announced. Project spokesman Garrett Nordstrom says flinthillsdigitalcampus.com was meant to be an informational site before rezoning and was meant to “dispel misconceptions.” Nordstrom says the website still exists but is internal now and is being shared with potential end users. Nordstrom says no end user has been selected for the proposed data center in west Emporia. He also says it would be unusual for a public website to document a private development project. The data center ballot questions will be part of KVOE’s political interviews later this month ahead of the general election Nov. 3. Appearing at 10:06 am Oct. 20 will be Vehige and Edgar Esparza from Emporia Neighbors United, as well as Woods representing Emporians for Progress. Our remaining interview slate is as follows: *Tuesday: Candidate Profile with Kansas House 13th District challenger Democrat Mark Remmert. Incumbent Republican Duane Droge did not confirm interest in a forum-style interview *Thursday: Candidate Forum with Kansas House 60th District challenger Democrat Maddison Glover and incumbent Republican Mark Schreiber *Oct 13: Candidate Forum with Kansas House 76th District nominees Democrat David Claridge and Republican Russel Stukey Click here for the KVOE Voter Information Guide courtesy Community National Bank & Trust.
