artigo.texto: To Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian, the debate over data centers starts with the boom in capital investment and property tax revenue the developments promise to the state. Creating regulatory guardrails on issues such as water usage and power are necessary but shouldn’t risk the potential return, Christian told the Fort Worth Report after appearing on a data centers panel Sept. 26 at the Texas Tribune’s annual TribFest conference in Austin. “I think you can learn from previous problems from data centers that have shown problems in the past,” said Christian, who doesn’t regulate data centers but has increasingly spoken on related questions about natural resources. “And what you do as an educated public is you fix the problems, you regulate to make sure it doesn’t happen again. But you don’t stop and turn down billions, billions of free market dollars.” Data centers — and their massive potential economic return — have careened into the intersection of the free market and community concerns about their environmental impact. The Texas Legislature is set to take up the debate over regulation in the 2027 session. The accompanying statistics highlight the choices and problems data center developers and operators face. Demand nationally for development of data centers — the buildings that house the digital infrastructure necessary for processing daily transactions worldwide for everything from paying water bills to buying airline tickets — is surging, according to research by the JLL commercial real estate firm. Seventy-nine percent of Americans support U.S. leadership in artificial intelligence, but only 14 percent support “data centers in our community,” according to research by JLL, Gallup and Reuters published by JLL in August. JLL declined a request by the Report for an interview for this story. Communities are experiencing the conundrum. In Fort Worth, property tax revenue makes up about 60% of the city’s general fund budget, which pays for most basic city services. But residential revenue — 63% of the tax base, compared to commercial — has turned soft in recent years because of protests and litigation, plus the Tarrant Appraisal District’s policy of reappraising every two years. Fort Worth struggled to close a $94 million budget shortfall for 2027 as a result. The city estimated this spring it received $83 million in gross property tax revenue from four data centers in the city over the last five years. In 2024, Fort Worth’s property tax revenue from data centers equaled the same revenue from 8,378 average-valued single family homes, the city estimated. “That’s a huge impact to a school district as well,” Jesica McEachern, an assistant city manager, told council members June 2 in presenting a report on proposed regulation. By 2030, including the existing data centers and phases of planned facilities the city projects will launch by then, the proportion of property tax taken up by commercial property could move more toward half, driven by the hubs, she estimated. It would take an estimated 22,718 average-valued single family homes in fiscal 2031 to generate the same projected property tax as data centers for that year, she added. McEachern maintained the economic benefit of data centers isn’t the “decision point” on whether to accept them. City officials have debated water, power, noise, land use, neighborhood encroachment, setbacks and other questions. Christian takes another view on the matter of decision points. Capital investment by investors in Texas artificial intelligence and data center projects now rivals investments in oil and gas, he noted. Some cities are now actively recruiting data center development. “Now, digest that total amount of money,” Christian said. “What that would do for future generations, for Texas, and for opportunities in half the state that’s literally dying. Here’s opportunities for families to have money, businesses, opportunities for the American dream to be expanded.” Looking ahead to what the Legislature may decide, Fort Worth City Council members in August unanimously approved the first move toward implementing a 90-day moratorium on the construction of data centers. Council members have struggled with the issue as throngs of residents have shown up at meetings to protest data center development. “Data centers can add significantly to the tax base, even if they create fewer permanent jobs than some other uses,” council member Michael Crain told the Report this week. “That’s why we need to evaluate each proposal on its merits — its long-term tax revenue, jobs, infrastructure demands and impact on nearby neighborhoods — and determine whether it’s the right fit for our community.” Data center developers and operators have descended on Texas, which has now overtaken Virginia as the nation’s top state for such projects, because of its business-friendly approach, low energy cost, faster permitting, incentives and abundance of land close to power infrastructure, Fort Worth city staff told council members at the June 2 meeting. Such projects also have low impact on city services and infrastructure, the staff said. After the staff presented the property tax comparison of data centers to single-family homes at the meeting, council member Macy Hill asked for information on the costs of providing infrastructure to homes compared to data centers. Whether to offer economic incentives, as the city often does in cases where major investment is being offered, has quickly become a flashpoint. “These are not desirable land uses,” council member Elizabeth Beck said at the meeting. “I think what makes them desirable is their tax base. So by giving that up to get them I think is a ridiculous policy. If they’re so needed, then they’ll come. And if they’re so needed and they need an incentive, they can go somewhere else.” Industry estimates on data center valuations for property tax purposes are significantly higher than for other potential commercial land uses. artigo.texto: Actis adds 244MW / 1,141MWh battery storage portfolio to Polish platform within three months of launch - Transaction advances Actis’ 1.5GW wind, solar, and BESS target for new Central & Eastern Europe platform - Actis has committed more than US$1.1 billion across three platforms in CEE LONDON, 6 October 2026: Actis, a leading growth market investor in sustainable infrastructure, today announced it is acquiring two battery energy storage system (BESS) projects as it rapidly scales its recently launched Polish renewable energy platform. The projects are being acquired from DRI, with one 112MW / 518MWh project in Kozienice already acquired and ready for construction by Actis, and the other – a 132MW / 623MWh project in Trzebinia – signed and set to complete once operational. These projects will represent some of the first utility-scale BESS projects to reach commercial operation in Poland, with a total 244MW of power capacity and 1,141MWh of four-hour plus duration energy storage. Both assets benefit from a secured revenue base through a 17-year inflation-indexed capacity market contract. Building on Actis’ acquisition of Klara Renewables – a 171MW onshore wind portfolio with approximately 275MW of hybridisation potential, signed in July 2026 – these two assets support Actis’ integrated approach, combining renewable power generation with BESS to create a system-level portfolio that aims to mitigate volatility and maximise value capture across the power system while increasing Poland’s grid flexibility and renewable energy integration capability. With Poland expected to retire approximately 18GW of coal while adding 50GW of renewables and 14GW of gas capacity by 2040, the country’s structural transition away from coal offers significant growth opportunities for assets like BESS, particularly given electricity demand is forecast to more than double by 2050 due to industrial and transport electrification and economic growth. This transformation is underpinned by attractive financial mechanisms, including a strong capacity market providing long-term and stable cashflows, alongside robust corporate PPA demand. Jaroslava Korpanec, Head of Central & Eastern Europe at Actis, commented: "The CEE region has historically been underinvested in, and the need to drive decarbonisation and invest in independent energy supply is, in our view, absolutely crucial. Poland is a major European power market but a carbon-intensive one that needs to transition from coal to renewables while keeping the grid steady. These two projects will help build the grid flexibility required and in doing so support Poland in managing its energy transition, energy competitiveness and resilience.” Murat Cinar, Chief Executive Officer of DRI, said: “Battery storage is expected to play an increasingly important role in Poland’s energy system as the share of renewables continues to grow. We believe Kozienice and Trzebinia are strong projects that can provide significant flexibility to the grid and we are pleased to see them moving into their next stage with Actis. This transaction also reflects the strength, in our view, of DRI’s capability to develop and advance meaningful energy projects in Europe’s most important growth markets.” ENDS RELATED ARTICLES The statements contained herein, including those made by Jaroslava Korpanec are as of 6 October 2026 and represent the views of Actis which is not research and should not be treated as research. artigo.texto: U.S. data center capacity growth projections appear to be on track for 2026 and 2027 despite mounting opposition to projects that support the build-out of artificial intelligence technologies. Goldman Sachs now projects that total U.S. data center capacity will reach 64 gigawatts by year’s end, an increase in its prior forecast by 5 gigawatts. But the financial services firm also decreased its 2027 forecast by 5 gigawatts, expecting it to reach 90 gigawatts in that year. U.S. capacity stands at about 62.7 gigawatts, according to energy data firm Cleanview. The latest big development announcements include plans in Virginia by LG Electronics to build its first U.S. plant focused on production of chillers for data center cooling. On the investment side, facility operator Sabey Data Center Properties reported a significant new commitment from global equity firm Ares Management Corp. to support expansion. Nearly 400 U.S. cities and towns, along with at least 14 states, are considering moratoriums or other restrictions on data center development. This comes as more than 1,500 data center projects are in various stages of planning nationwide, according to the Pew Research Center. “While U.S. data center development faces increasing political and community opposition, project data and our updated capacity estimates suggest that the U.S. data center growth outlook through 2027 remains largely unchanged,” Goldman analysts said in a research note issued Sunday. Goldman’s 2026-2027 projections are based on its forecast of a 38% increase in U.S. power demand in 2026 and another 38% rise in 2027, much of it driven by data centers. A single gigawatt is roughly enough to power up to around 1 million homes, based on energy industry standards. Power consumption plays a big part in nationwide opposition to data centers, with communities concerned about energy, water and land usage amid worries that projects could also drive up utility bills for residents and businesses near the facilities. Several technology and energy firms have pledged to pay costs for needed utility upgrades as states and cities seek to put those policies into law. Data center projects increasingly include on-site power generation facilities designed to prevent taking power from regional grids, but those components add considerably to development costs. Goldman previously projected that U.S. capital investment in data centers and related AI support systems would hit $765 billion for 2026 alone. The firm expects cumulative global capital spending to reach $7.6 trillion by 2031. More companies boost investment Much of the current and future spending is coming from the largest tech company “hyperscalers,” such as Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Facebook parent Meta. Multiple other data center operators, investors and suppliers are responding to the AI build-out. LG Electronics, a division of the South Korean industrial giant, said it is expanding its global chiller manufacturing capacity with its first facility in the U.S., planned for a 43-acre site near Windsor in southeastern Virginia. Production is scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027 at a 350,000-square-foot industrial building completed in 2025 by developers of the Shirley T. Holland Intermodal Park, according to an LG statement and regional reports. The new plant is expected to employ more than 150 people and is part of LG Electronics’ strategy to "expand production capacity for advanced cooling technologies and better serve the rapidly expanding customer base in North America,” Don Kwack, CEO of LG Electronics North America, said in the statement. LG plans to invest more than $100 million in the new U.S. facility and expansions of two existing South Korean factories to meet North American demand, the company said. Its first U.S. chiller factory “is addressing the growing need for advanced cooling solutions for data centers across the country,” said Chris Ahn, president of LG Electronics USA’s air conditioning technology division. In another transaction, leaders of Sabey Data Center Properties, the operator of more than 4 million square feet of U.S. data centers, announced on Monday an expanded investment by minority owner Ares Management Corp. That takes the equity firm’s stake to more than $500 million since the first investment was announced in July. Sabey Data Center Properties is majority-owned by Seattle-based Sabey Corp. and National Real Estate Advisors LLC of Washington, D.C. A statement from the two companies and Los Angeles-based Ares said new funding will go toward planned U.S. capacity expansion by Sabey Data Center Properties. Sabey’s development pipeline would take its data center computing capacity from its current 275 megawatts to a planned 737 megawatts by 2033, company officials said. A single megawatt powers up to about 1,000 homes, according to industry standards.

artigo.texto: New data center development in Anne Arundel County is on hold while county leaders decide how to regulate the rapidly growing industry. The Anne Arundel County Council voted 7-0 Monday night to approve an amended version of Bill 63-26, establishing a temporary moratorium on new data center development. The moratorium will run until Jan. 31, 2028, or until the county adopts comprehensive data center legislation, whichever comes first. The measure differs significantly from the bill as originally introduced. Council members initially considered banning new privately operated data centers in the county, then unanimously amended the proposal in September to replace the ban with a temporary moratorium. Projects already in the development process will generally be allowed to continue. The amended measure also includes future phases of existing data centers on adjacent or adjoining properties. During the moratorium, the county will establish a work group to study data center development and recommend permanent regulations to the county executive and County Council. The group is expected to consider energy and water use, utility infrastructure, noise, air quality, environmental impacts, and economic development. The debate comes as data centers continue to expand in Anne Arundel County. Microsoft, which is developing a data center campus at Annapolis Junction Business Park, previously testified against the original ban. The company said it supported developing regulations and creating a work group, but wanted existing campuses to continue development. The legislation also calls for repealing a personal property tax assessment reduction for qualified data storage centers. This is a developing story, so check back with WMAR2News.com for updates. artigo.texto: Kandi secures CATL order: Kandi Technologies Group stock is valued at USD 68.6 million Published on 10/05/2026 at 01:02 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS Kandi Technologies Group, Inc. (ISIN VGG5214E1034) secured a follow-on order for CATL heavy-truck battery-swap stations on September 28, 2026, as Kandi Technologies Group stock carried a USD 68.6 million market capitalization on October 2, 2026. The order marked the second batch tied to the company partnership with CATL within two months, according to Kandi Technologies. Battery swapping adds a second engine Kandi's China Battery Exchange subsidiary is building a battery-swapping equipment business alongside its electric off-road vehicle operations. The September 28 order gives that newer activity another commercial deployment milestone, while the company continues to sell utility vehicles, neighborhood electric vehicles, golf carts and off-road products. The CATL relationship matters because the follow-on order connects Kandi to heavy-truck infrastructure rather than only consumer and recreational mobility. The September 28 announcement therefore broadens the operating narrative from vehicle manufacturing toward equipment supplied for commercial transport. First-half revenue rose 57.4 percent For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Kandi reported USD 57.1 million of net revenue, up 57.4 percent from USD 36.3 million in the comparable period of 2025, according to StockTitan. Revenue from off-road vehicles and related parts increased 59.4 percent to USD 54.2 million, making that business the main quantified driver in the interim report. Gross profit rose 51.5 percent to USD 24.8 million in the first half of 2026, while gross margin eased to 43.5 percent from 45.2 percent. The combination shows faster sales growth alongside a modest contraction in gross profitability. Operating income turned positive Kandi reported USD 5.5 million of operating income for the first half of 2026, compared with a USD 1.9 million operating loss in the same period of 2025. Net income increased 452.2 percent to USD 9.4 million from USD 1.7 million, and diluted earnings per share reached USD 0.10 versus USD 0.02. The figures put operating execution beside the CATL order as the central issue for the company. Cash, restricted cash and certificates of deposit totaled USD 285.7 million as of June 30, 2026, while total assets stood at USD 461.4 million. Market value remains compact Kandi's market capitalization was USD 68.6 million as of October 2, 2026. The company is listed on Nasdaq under KNDI and operates in the consumer cyclical sector, with the industry classification Auto - Manufacturers. artigo.texto: Ecopro BM said on Monday it signed a memorandum of understanding with Samsung SDI to cooperate on developing materials for all-solid-state batteries. The two companies will begin joint research and development with the goal of commercialising sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries in 2027. They plan to establish a cooperation system from early development through quality evaluation and building a mass-production system. Samsung SDI will take charge of developing all-solid-state battery cells and advancing mass-production technology, while Ecopro BM will be responsible for developing key materials. The cooperation will cover a range of key materials, starting with cathode materials and including electrolytes for cathodes and electrolytes for separators. All-solid-state batteries are seen as next-generation technology that can improve safety and performance. They are cited as a core technology for electric vehicles and humanoid robots because they can be used longer on a single charge and have a lower fire risk. Ecopro BM has secured proprietary process technology in the field of sulfide-based solid electrolytes. It is also operating a pilot plant with annual capacity of 40 tons, the company said. Based on competitiveness in powder-control and quality-management technologies, it is also developing cathode materials suitable for solid electrolytes on the back of its high-nickel cathode material technology. On the back of these results, Ecopro BM was selected in August for the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy's "Super Eul" project. The project is an R&D support programme aimed at fostering materials, parts and equipment companies that will lead global supply chains by securing world-leading and first-of-its-kind technologies. Companies propose growth strategies and technology development plans, and selections are made through plan evaluation, technology verification and comprehensive assessment. Ecopro BM passed evaluation with a sulfide-based solid-electrolyte task, and the government plans to support selected companies for at least 7 years with 20 billion won per task. Kong Bo-hyun (공보현), an executive director in charge of research and development at Ecopro BM, said at the time on solid-electrolyte development, "We are currently reviewing pilot mass production with leading customers, and we expect the earliest mass-production timing to be 2027. We have completed mass-production line design and are preparing so that we can immediately begin construction in line with customer demand."

artigo.texto: Demanda por Interconexão de Data Centers de IA Dispara: Quais Ações de Comunicação Óptica Mais se Beneficiam? 5 Ações dos EUA para Acompanhar A expansão dos data centers de IA impulsiona a demanda por infraestrutura de transmissão de dados de alta velocidade, priorizando conexões ópticas sobre cabos de cobre para evitar gargalos nas GPUs. Cinco empresas destacam-se nesse mercado: Lumentum, Coherent, Applied Optoelectronics, Credo Technology e Ciena. Lumentum lidera em crescimento de componentes ópticos; Coherent oferece um portfólio diversificado e escala; Applied Optoelectronics apresenta alta elasticidade em módulos de 800G e 1,6T; Credo destaca-se por margens elevadas em chips de conectividade; e Ciena foca em redes ópticas de grande escala para data centers. TradingKey - A competição nos data centers de IA está se expandindo para além do simples aumento no número de GPUs, voltando-se para o aprimoramento da eficiência da transmissão de dados em todo o cluster de computação. À medida que milhares ou mesmo dezenas de milhares de aceleradores de IA são conectados em um único cluster, os cabos de cobre tradicionais enfrentam limitações crescentes em distância de transmissão, largura de banda e consumo de energia, impulsionando o desenvolvimento acelerado de tecnologias como módulos ópticos de 800G e 1,6T, comutação óptica e óptica co-empacotada. A comunicação óptica para IA refere-se à transmissão de informações por meio de sinais ópticos entre chips, servidores, racks e data centers. Em comparação com as conexões tradicionais de cobre, as conexões ópticas oferecem vantagens na transmissão a longas distâncias, alta largura de banda e controle de eficiência energética, tornando-se particularmente adequadas para os clusters de computação de IA em constante expansão. O treinamento de grandes modelos de IA não é realizado de forma independente por uma única GPU; em vez disso, exige um vasto conjunto de processadores trocando parâmetros e dados continuamente. Quando as velocidades de transmissão de rede não acompanham o ritmo das velocidades de computação, as GPUs podem ficar ociosas à espera de dados. Como resultado, os data centers de IA exigem não apenas mais chips, mas também atualizações sincronizadas em switches, chips de conectividade, módulos ópticos, lasers e sistemas de redes ópticas. Em comparação com a computação em nuvem tradicional, o treinamento de IA exige a transmissão frequente de volumes massivos de dados entre servidores. Se a velocidade da rede não acompanhar o poder de processamento das GPUs, até mesmo os chips mais caros podem não operar em capacidade máxima por ficarem aguardando a chegada dos dados. Consequentemente, a comunicação óptica está deixando de ser um simples equipamento de suporte para se tornar um componente vital da infraestrutura de IA. No mercado de ações dos EUA, a Coherent (COHR), a Lumentum (LITE), a Credo Technology (CRDO), a Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI) e a Ciena (CIEN) são atualmente ações representativas no segmento de interconexão de alta velocidade para IA. No entanto, as cinco empresas diferem em seu posicionamento de negócios, abrangendo componentes ópticos, módulos ópticos, chips de conectividade, sistemas de redes ópticas e equipamentos de interconexão para data centers. Lumentum: Fornecedora Principal de Componentes Ópticos de Alta Velocidade e Lasers A Lumentum vem se tornando uma das empresas de crescimento mais rápido no atual ciclo de comunicação óptica para IA. Seus produtos abrangem componentes de comunicação óptica, módulos ópticos para nuvem, sistemas de comutação de circuitos ópticos e lasers de alta potência necessários para a tecnologia de óptica empacotada (co-packaged optics). A receita recém-divulgada pela Lumentum para o quarto trimestre do ano fiscal de 2026 atingiu US$ 1,006 bilhão, uma alta de 109,3% na comparação anual, com lucro por ação não-GAAP de US$ 3,23. A empresa projeta que a receita do primeiro trimestre do ano fiscal de 2027 alcance de US$ 1,225 bilhão a US$ 1,275 bilhão, indicando que a demanda por comunicações ópticas de alta velocidade continua crescendo rapidamente. Mais importante ainda, a diretoria da Lumentum declarou explicitamente que, à medida que as cargas de trabalho de computação de IA exigem maior velocidade e largura de banda, a arquitetura dos data centers está se voltando para a conectividade óptica. A empresa está avançando em produtos relacionados à tecnologia 1,6T e expandindo sua presença em soluções de conectividade óptica. A força da Lumentum reside em seus componentes essenciais de comunicação óptica e tecnologia laser, garantindo-lhe maior sensibilidade às mudanças na demanda por interconexão óptica de alta velocidade em comparação com fabricantes dedicados exclusivamente a equipamentos para data centers. No entanto, a LITE tornou-se uma ação de infraestrutura de IA amplamente monitorada, apresentando alta volatilidade no preço de suas ações e em seu valuation. Consequentemente, qualquer desaceleração nas expectativas de alto crescimento pode exercer uma pressão significativa sobre o seu valuation. artigo.texto: Explainer: Why Some Indian Exporters Have To Pay Europe For Carbon Emissions In India The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism puts a carbon cost on imports, calculated per tonne per product. Published : October 3, 2026 at 6:17 PM IST New Delhi: India and the European Union committed to increasing trade by concluding negotiations on the long-pending Free Trade Agreement, labelled the "mother of all deals," early this year. But as the two-decade-long negotiations drew to a close, a wrinkle emerged in the form of the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which sets a cost on products that release a large amount of greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide, during manufacturing. The CBAM came into full force on January 1, raising the possibility of higher export costs and potential diversification away from the EU market for carbon-intensive exports. Officials on both sides have continued discussions on the CBAM, ranging from how India's own carbon pricing policy will be factored into the carbon price to how emissions will be calculated. So as the two countries look to deepen trade, will CBAM prove to be a drag on carbon-intensive Indian exports like steel to the EU? Why are companies paying for emissions in India in the EU? The EU has the world’s biggest emissions trading market in its Emissions Trading System, which accounts for three-quarters of international carbon trading. Within this, the CBAM is a mechanism that puts a carbon cost on imports, calculated per tonne per product. CBAM is applied to carbon-intensive products such as iron, steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen, and electricity imported into the EU. On steel, for instance, the rate will be calculated according to the carbon intensity of the specific steel production multiplied by the EU Emissions Trading System which is around €70–€80 per tonne of carbon dioxide (CO₂) with any free allocations and carbon price paid domestically also factored into the final Carbon rate. The EU implemented the definitive CBAM regime from January 1 this year to put non-EU manufacturers on par with domestic ones who pay carbon rates. But importers will only have to start submitting the CBAM certificates next year, with annual declarations by September. In order to implement CBAM, manufacturers first calculate the carbon emitted per tonne of production and then report the emissions. Importers are required to buy CBAM certificates to cover those emissions. Put simply, an Indian steel producer, exporting to the EU, will provide verified emissions data or carbon emitted per tonne of production to the EU importer who would then calculate the carbon rate and buy CBAM certificates for the corresponding carbon rates. The importer will then submit the certificate as payment. Though CBAM costs are paid by the importers, the cost is passed down to non-EU exporters or manufacturers in the form of lower prices or reduced margins for importers. If the EU finds incorrect emission details have been submitted, the fine includes €100 per tonne of Co2 equivalent. A key aim of the CBAM for the EU is to prevent carbon leakage or prevent companies from moving production overseas to countries with less stringent climate rules. Indian exporters to feel the carbon pinch While India’s CBAM-exposed exports to the EU account for only 0.2 per cent of its GDP, the iron and steel sector constitutes 90 per cent of these exports, making the sector "particularly vulnerable", according to a report by think tank Centre for Social and Economic Progress (CSEP). India exports around $75.85 billion worth of goods to the EU with 10 per cent of this attracting CBAM for now. India is taking steps to strengthen preparedness for the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), with a focus on compliance, emissions data, verification and exporter awareness. From industry engagement and training to work on steel emission data, verifier accreditation… pic.twitter.com/5B1sm2w1cQ — Dept of Commerce, GoI (@DoC_GoI) September 29, 2026 According to CSEP, Indian steel exports are vulnerable due to the industry’s relatively higher carbon footprint compared to their European counterparts. For instance, India averages roughly 2.3 to 2.5 tonnes of CO₂ per tonne of crude steel, higher than the EU benchmark of 1.37 and world average benchmark of 1.92. Studies and analysts believe that, as a result of the CBAM smaller manufacturers who operate on smaller margins may not be able to pay the cost of decarbonising their business. Analysts also believe that exporters might look for alternative markets that do not have such a carbon pricing policy. According to an estimate by the Global Trade Research, CBAM will force Indian steel and aluminium exporters to slash prices by 15 to 22 per cent to stay competitive. Why is CBAM linked to climate justice? Beyond the trade aspect, there is a larger issue concerning CBAM. International treaties have recognised that developed countries have a greater responsibility towards climate change as they contributed the most and have more resources to adopt clean technologies and create solutions. The criticism is that revenue under CBAM moves away from developing nations and emerging economies, which require climate funds, into the EU, which is imposing its environmental standards on countries that have different levels of development. So the question is whether developed nations, that share a larger burden of historical emissions and pollution, should face the CBAM. India has criticised the CBAM as arbitrary and a protectionist non-tariff trade barrier that violates core multilateral trade rules at the World Trade Organisation (WTO). While India is engaged in CBAM discussions with the EU, it is closely tracking proceedings brought by Russia at the WTO against the CBAM alleging it is a trade barrier and an export subsidy under the EU emissions trading system. artigo.texto: Air Liquide Major player in hydrogen infrastructure According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Hydrogen Storage Materials market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global hydrogen storage materials market is positioned for transformative growth through 2035, driven by the urgent need for bankable long-duration energy storage and the scaling of hydrogen mobility. This market, encompassing solid-state materials and engineered systems that store hydrogen via adsorption or chemical bonding, is evolving from niche technology demonstration to commercial deployment. Demand is bifurcating: high-performance, high-cost materials serve mobility applications such as fuel cell vehicles, aviation, and maritime, while cost-optimized, scalable materials target stationary energy storage. Material selection is increasingly a systems engineering decision, influenced by balance-of-plant complexity, power conversion compatibility, and thermal management. Supply chain resilience remains a critical bottleneck due to dependencies on rare earth elements and specialized alloys, exposing the market to geopolitical risks. The qualification and certification burden is immense, particularly for mobility and large-scale stationary storage, creating time-to-market barriers that favor established players. Project economics for hydrogen-based long-duration storage are currently dominated by electrolyzer and power conversion costs, placing intense pressure on storage material costs to achieve total system bankability. The competitive landscape is fragmenting into advanced material specialists, integrated system providers, and energy majors, with channel control shifting toward those offering certified, bankable sub-systems. Regional strategies diverge, with some geographies acting as demand hubs and others as manufacturing hubs, creating complex trade flows and local content requirements. The baseline scenario for the hydrogen storage materials market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates robust expansion, underpinned by the global energy transition and the imperative to decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors. The market is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 18.5%, reaching a market index of 450 by 2035 (2025=100). This growth is not uniform; it is characterized by a bifurcation between mobility and stationary storage applications. In mobility, demand is driven by fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs), buses, trucks, and maritime vessels, where high gravimetric and volumetric density are paramount, favoring metal hydrides and complex hydrides despite higher costs. In stationary storage, the focus is on long-duration energy storage (LDES) to support renewable integration, where cost per kilowatt-hour and cycle life are critical, driving adoption of lower-cost materials and engineered systems. The supply chain will face significant challenges, including limited high-volume production of specialized alloy powders and dependence on critical minerals like rare earth elements. However, these challenges also spur innovation in alternative chemistries and recycling. The qualification and certification burden will remain a key barrier, but as standards evolve and more materials achieve certification, the market will broaden. Project economics will improve as scale and manufacturing efficiencies reduce costs, but the pace of growth will be sensitive to policy support, hydrogen infrastructure build-out, and the cost of competing technologies like lithium-ion batteries. Overall, the market is poised for a decade of dynamic growth, with significant opportunities for companies that can navigate the technical and commercial complexities. The mobility sector represents the most dynamic and demanding application for hydrogen storage materials. Currently, fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs), buses, and trucks rely predominantly on compressed hydrogen tanks (Type IV), but solid-state materials offer the potential for higher volumetric density, lower pressure, and improved safety. Through 2035, as FCEV adoption accelerates in heavy-duty transport, maritime, and aviation, demand for advanced metal hydrides and complex hydrides will surge. Key demand-side indicators include vehicle production volumes, refueling infrastructure build-out, and total cost of ownership parity with diesel. The mechanism is straightforward: as fleet operators seek zero-emission solutions with long range and fast refueling, hydrogen storage materials that enable compact, lightweight, and safe onboard storage become critical. However, cost and durability remain challenges, with ongoing R&D focused on reducing material costs and improving cycle life. The sector's growth will be punctuated by regional differences, with Asia-Pacific leading in FCEV deployment, followed by Europe and North America. Current trend: Rapid growth driven by decarbonization targets and expanding model availability.. Major trends: Shift toward heavy-duty FCEVs and buses, requiring higher capacity storage, Development of low-pressure, high-density storage systems for maritime and aviation, Increasing partnerships between material suppliers and OEMs for integrated storage solutions, and Government mandates and subsidies for zero-emission commercial vehicles. Representative participants: Toyota Motor Corporation, Hyundai Motor Company, Nikola Corporation, Ballard Power Systems Inc, Cummins Inc, and Hexagon Purus ASA. The stationary power sector, including utilities and grid operators, is increasingly turning to hydrogen storage materials for long-duration energy storage (LDES) to balance renewable intermittency and provide backup power. Currently, deployment is limited to pilot projects and demonstration plants, but through 2035, as renewable penetration exceeds 50% in many regions, the need for cost-effective, scalable LDES will drive significant demand. artigo.texto: Mercado global de réguas de tomadas múltiplas: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Mercado global de réguas de tomadas múltiplas: projeção até 2035 aponta crescimento de 6% a 9% ao ano impulsionado por data centers e energias renováveis Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de réguas de tomadas múltiplas, o setor entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado mundial de réguas de tomadas múltiplas deve crescer a uma taxa composta anual de 6% a 9% entre 2026 e 2035, alcançando um índice de mercado de 185 (2025=100). Esse avanço é sustentado pela aceleração das adições de capacidade em armazenamento de energia renovável, implantação de data centers e sistemas industriais de backup, nos quais as réguas atuam como nós críticos de distribuição final. As unidades de grau premium vendidas a integradores de laboratórios biomédicos e farmacêuticos alcançam prêmios de preço de 40% a 80% sobre os modelos comerciais padrão, refletindo exigências rigorosas de isolamento de grau hospitalar, proteção contra surtos e certificação de conformidade. A dependência de importações supera 60% da oferta total do mercado na maioria dos centros de demanda fora da Ásia, com China e Taiwan respondendo por mais de três quartos da capacidade global de produção e montagem. O mercado caminha para unidades de distribuição de energia gerenciadas e de alta densidade, que integram monitoramento remoto, medição por tomada e lógica de alívio de carga para sistemas modulares de armazenamento de energia em baterias e módulos pré-fabricados de data center. No entanto, a volatilidade dos custos de insumos como fio de cobre, plásticos antichama e componentes eletrônicos de proteção contra surtos gera pressão recorrente sobre as margens, enquanto os atrasos na certificação ampliam os prazos de entrega em 8 a 16 semanas para o lançamento de novos produtos. Este relatório oferece uma visão orientada por dados da dinâmica de mercado, do cenário competitivo e das projeções até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado mundial de réguas de tomadas múltiplas projeta um CAGR de 6% a 9% entre 2026 e 2035, com o índice de mercado subindo para 185 (2025=100). Essa perspectiva pressupõe a continuidade da expansão da construção de data centers, das adições de capacidade de energia renovável e da automação industrial, que em conjunto impulsionam a demanda por distribuição de energia confiável e de alta densidade. Espera-se que o mercado se beneficie do ciclo de substituição da infraestrutura elétrica envelhecida nas economias desenvolvidas e de novas instalações nos mercados emergentes. No entanto, o crescimento será moderado pela volatilidade dos preços das matérias-primas, especialmente cobre e plásticos antichama, que podem oscilar entre 15% e 25% em um horizonte de dois anos. A diversificação da cadeia de suprimentos para longe da China e de Taiwan deve reduzir gradualmente a dependência de importações, mas as exigências de certificação e documentação de qualidade continuarão sendo um gargalo. A transição para réguas inteligentes, com monitoramento, carregamento USB e controle individual de tomadas, criará segmentos premium, sobretudo em ambientes biomédicos e laboratoriais. No geral, o mercado está preparado para uma expansão constante, com a Ásia-Pacífico mantendo sua liderança em produção e consumo, enquanto América do Norte e Europa se concentram em produtos certificados de alto valor. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Expansão acelerada da capacidade de data centers e instalações de computação de borda, exigindo unidades de distribuição de energia de alta densidade com monitoramento remoto e medição por tomada. - Implantação acelerada de sistemas de armazenamento de energia renovável, nos quais as réguas atuam como nós de distribuição final entre inversores, racks de baterias e sistemas de monitoramento. - Crescimento da demanda por soluções industriais de backup e resiliência na indústria de transformação, motivado pela necessidade de proteger equipamentos sensíveis contra interrupções de energia. - Adoção crescente de portas de carregamento USB em ambientes residenciais e comerciais, impulsionando a procura por réguas com múltiplas tomadas e carregamento USB integrado. - Exigências rigorosas de segurança e certificação em laboratórios biomédicos e farmacêuticos, elevando a demanda por réguas de grau premium com isolamento de grau hospitalar e proteção contra surtos. - Ciclo de substituição da infraestrutura elétrica envelhecida nas economias desenvolvidas, sobretudo na América do Norte e na Europa, sustentando a demanda do mercado de reposição. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Volatilidade dos preços de matérias-primas, especialmente fio de cobre e plásticos antichama, que podem oscilar entre 15% e 25% em um horizonte de dois anos, pressionando as margens. - Atrasos na certificação em laboratórios de ensaio ampliam os prazos de entrega em 8 a 16 semanas para o lançamento de novos produtos, sobretudo nos segmentos biomédico e de energia renovável. - Ciclos longos de compra em grandes projetos de infraestrutura, frequentemente superiores a 12 meses, exigindo que os fornecedores mantenham estoques amplos em meio a especificações em constante mudança. - Concorrência intensa de fabricantes de baixo custo na Ásia, gerando pressão de preços e comoditização nos segmentos de réguas básicas. - Tarifas e barreiras comerciais que afetam as cadeias de suprimentos transfronteiriças, elevando custos e complicando as estratégias de compra nas regiões dependentes de importações. artigo.texto: Tesla Powerwall, Megapack According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Battery Storage Racks market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global battery storage racks market is entering a phase of sustained expansion, underpinned by the accelerating deployment of energy storage systems across utility, commercial, and residential applications. Battery storage racks are engineered structural frameworks that securely house, organize, and support battery modules, integrating thermal management, wiring, and safety components. As renewable energy penetration rises and grid operators seek flexibility, the demand for robust, modular, and containerized rack solutions is intensifying. The market is characterized by a diverse competitive landscape, ranging from specialized engineering firms to diversified industrial manufacturers and system integrators. Between 2026 and 2035, growth will be propelled by utility-scale storage projects, data center UPS requirements, and the proliferation of residential solar-plus-storage systems. However, supply chain volatility, evolving safety standards, and intense price competition present notable challenges. This report provides a data-driven analysis of market size, segmentation, regional dynamics, and key trends, offering stakeholders a transparent view of the opportunities and risks shaping the industry's trajectory through 2035. The baseline scenario for the world battery storage racks market anticipates robust growth from 2026 to 2035, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.2%, reaching a market index of 220 by 2035 (2025=100). This outlook assumes continued policy support for renewable energy, declining battery costs, and rapid expansion of utility-scale storage capacity. The market's expansion is closely tied to global energy storage installations, which are projected to multiply several times over the forecast period. Stationary and containerized racks will dominate demand, particularly for grid-scale projects, while modular and rack-mounted systems gain traction in commercial and residential segments. Asia-Pacific will remain the largest market, driven by China's aggressive storage targets, followed by North America and Europe. Supply chain constraints for steel and aluminum, along with logistical bottlenecks, may temper growth in the short term, but innovation in materials and modular designs will enhance cost efficiency. The competitive landscape is expected to consolidate, with larger players leveraging scale and integrated solutions. Overall, the market is poised for a period of dynamic expansion, with significant opportunities for manufacturers that can offer standardized, safety-compliant, and thermally optimized rack solutions. Utility-scale energy storage is the largest and fastest-growing end-use segment for battery storage racks, driven by the global shift toward renewable energy and the need for grid stability. These projects require large-scale, containerized or stationary racks that can house thousands of battery modules, often in harsh outdoor environments. Demand is propelled by national renewable portfolio standards, capacity auctions, and declining battery costs. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the integration of solar and wind farms, where storage racks are essential for smoothing output and providing peak capacity. Key demand-side indicators include the volume of utility-scale storage projects announced, grid interconnection queues, and government tenders. The trend is toward higher energy density, modular designs for faster installation, and integrated thermal management to ensure safety and longevity. Major companies supplying racks for this segment include Vertiv, Eaton, and Sungrow, often in partnership with battery manufacturers and EPC contractors. Current trend: Rapid expansion. Major trends: Shift toward containerized and modular rack systems for faster deployment, Integration of advanced thermal management and fire suppression within racks, Increasing use of steel and aluminum alloys for lightweight, corrosion-resistant structures, Standardization of rack designs to reduce costs and lead times, and Growing adoption of digital monitoring and predictive maintenance features. Representative participants: Vertiv Holdings, Eaton Corporation, Sungrow Power Supply, Fluence Energy, Tesla Inc, and BYD Company. Commercial and industrial (C&I) backup power applications are a significant driver of battery storage rack demand, as businesses seek to ensure operational continuity amid grid instability and rising energy costs. These systems typically require modular or rack-mounted battery configurations that can be scaled to match facility load profiles. Demand is particularly strong in regions with unreliable grid infrastructure, as well as in sectors such as manufacturing, healthcare, and retail, where power interruptions can cause substantial financial losses. Through 2035, the segment will expand as more companies adopt on-site storage to manage demand charges, participate in demand response programs, and integrate renewable generation. Key indicators include commercial construction activity, electricity price volatility, and the adoption of energy-as-a-service models. Rack solutions for C&I must balance compactness, safety, and ease of installation, often incorporating integrated power management hardware. Companies like Schneider Electric, ABB, and Rittal are prominent in this space. Current trend: Steady growth. Major trends: Growing adoption of behind-the-meter storage for demand charge management, Integration of racks with building management systems for smart energy control, Increased focus on safety and code compliance in urban installations, Rise of energy-as-a-service models reducing upfront costs for businesses, and Modular rack designs enabling incremental capacity expansion. artigo.texto: Siga o Times Brasil - Licenciado Exclusivo CNBC no AWS anuncia US$ 1 bi para enfrentar críticas ao uso de energia em data centers Publicado 04/10/2026 • 18:00 | Atualizado há 2 dias CEO da Nokia afirma que data centers seriam construídos “duas vezes mais rápido” sem restrições de fornecimento Ações brasileiras disparam com Bolsonaro agora visto como grande favorito para vencer a presidência Nasdaq bate novo recorde com alta das ações de tecnologia, apesar da pressão dos Treasuries Chefe da Saudi Aramco diz que recomposição dos estoques globais de petróleo pode levar dois anos Executivos da Anthropic, OpenAI, Google e Meta devem depor em audiência do Conselho Municipal de Nova York sobre os riscos da IA KEY POINTS Foto: wikimedia commons A Amazon Web Services (AWS) anunciou nesta sexta-feira (2) que investirá mais de US$ 1 bilhão nos próximos cinco anos em comunidades dos Estados Unidos que abrigam seus data centers. A iniciativa busca responder às críticas relacionadas ao consumo de energia elétrica e água dessas estruturas. Os centros de dados concentram a capacidade computacional necessária para treinar e executar modelos de inteligência artificial (I.A). Com a expansão dessa tecnologia, essas instalações passaram a enfrentar resistência em diferentes regiões dos Estados Unidos, principalmente por causa da demanda por eletricidade, dos custos dos serviços públicos e dos impactos sobre os recursos locais. Leia também: Amazon anuncia mais de US$ 1 bilhão para comunidades que abrigam centros de dados de IA Além disso, o anúncio ocorre poucas semanas antes das eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos, marcadas para 3 de novembro. A reação às novas estruturas de processamento de dados se tornou um desafio político para os republicanos no período que antecede a votação. O novo plano da AWS prevê recursos para áreas como educação, capacitação profissional, acesso a energia a preços acessíveis e conservação de água e energia. Os investimentos serão direcionados às comunidades onde a empresa mantém sua infraestrutura. A companhia também afirmou que pretende reduzir os impactos relacionados ao funcionamento dos data centers. Em comunicado, a AWS rebateu críticas sobre os efeitos ambientais, energéticos e econômicos dessas instalações. A Amazon destacou ainda que mais de 100 moratórias para novos data centers estão em análise nos Estados Unidos. As medidas mostram a resistência encontrada pela expansão dessas estruturas em diferentes comunidades do país. Siga o Times | CNBC no Google e receba as principais notícias do Brasil e do Mundo. Siga o Times | CNBC O novo aporte ocorre após uma expansão bilionária da infraestrutura da Amazon. A companhia informou ter investido US$ 276 bilhões em data centers entre 2011 e 2025. Além disso, a empresa mantém grandes projetos ou ampliações em estados como Indiana, Louisiana, Carolina do Norte, Virgínia e Mississippi. A expansão acompanha o crescimento da demanda por capacidade computacional para serviços de inteligência artificial. Para a AWS, a construção dessas estruturas tem caráter estratégico. Matt Garman, presidente-executivo da divisão de computação em nuvem da Amazon, afirmou que existe urgência na expansão porque os países que liderarem o desenvolvimento da inteligência artificial terão influência sobre a tecnologia e poderão aproveitar seus efeitos econômicos e de segurança nacional. A Amazon também reforçou o compromisso de alcançar uma operação positiva em água em todos os seus data centers até 2030. A meta prevê devolver às comunidades uma quantidade de água superior ao volume utilizado pelas instalações. Leia também: De resíduo a energia: Unicamp e Bionow transformam alcatrão em fonte renovável Segundo a AWS, 75% desse objetivo já foi alcançado. A medida faz parte dos esforços apresentados pela companhia para reduzir os impactos ambientais associados à expansão dos data centers. Com o avanço da inteligência artificial, a AWS amplia a capacidade computacional de seus data centers, o que aumenta a pressão sobre a infraestrutura de energia e os recursos hídricos. artigo.texto: Hyderabad-based Cygni Energy Pvt Ltd, an energy storage technology and manufacturing company, and Indus Towers Ltd, a telecom tower infrastructure provider, have collaborated to explore the sourcing of energy storage solutions for telecom infrastructure in India. In a press release, the companies said they have entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore setting up up to 1.5 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing capacity. The collaboration aims to address the evolving energy requirements of telecom infrastructure in India. The collaboration is also expected to evaluate advanced battery technologies for telecom applications, with the aim of enhancing reliability, improving energy efficiency, and enabling more sustainable telecom operations. The partnership represents a growing collaboration between technology developers, infrastructure providers, and manufacturing companies, particularly as India strengthens the integration of its digital and energy infrastructure. For the energy sector, such collaborations could support indigenous innovation, strengthen supply-chain resilience, and accelerate the adoption of next-generation energy storage solutions. Cygni Aligns With BESS Gigafactory Target Last year, Cygni Energy commenced Phase I of its BESS gigafactory. In 2025, Cygni Energy shared plans to set up a 160,000 sq. ft. Phase-I facility on a 5-acre campus, with a planned capacity of 4.8 GWh for battery packs for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. With an investment of over ₹100 crore, the facility was planned to cater to large-scale stationary storage projects and independent power producers (IPPs). Cygni Energy has also been working on India-specific sodium-ion-based energy storage solutions in collaboration with Chinese battery technology company HiNa Battery Technologies. The partnership focuses on developing sodium-ion solutions that can offer lower costs, improved safety, and faster charging capabilities, including charging times of around 20 minutes. Telecom-BESS Growing Nexus Commenting on the latest partnership, Venkat Rajaraman, Founder & CEO, Cygni Energy, said, “For us, this initiative goes beyond supplying batteries. It is about building the scale, technology capabilities and manufacturing readiness required to support the evolving energy needs of one of the world’s largest passive telecom infrastructure companies.” Rajaraman added, “We plan to develop capacity of up to 2 GWh, while building a portfolio that can evolve from today’s 100Ah solutions to higher-capacity 314Ah systems and emerging battery technologies. Our ambition is to combine scale, reliability and Indian engineering to create future-ready energy storage solutions that can evolve alongside India’s rapidly expanding digital infrastructure.” Commenting on the significance of such collaborations, Ashok Jhunjhunwala, Institute Professor, IIT Madras, and Chairman, ITEL Foundation, said, “Collaboration between users, startups, manufacturers and technology institutions can support the development and adoption of energy storage solutions in India. Telecom provides an important application for advancing battery technologies and manufacturing capabilities in this space.”

artigo.texto: O Mercado Voluntário de Carbono (MVC) passa a contar com três metodologias, em Portugal. O objetivo passa por reduzir as emissões carbónicas para a atmosfera, por forma a gerar créditos de carbono. Por decisão do Ministério do Ambiente e Energia, foram aprovadas duas novas metodologias de carbono dedicadas à Reflorestação e à Gestão Florestal Melhorada, que se juntam à já existente metodologia para Novas Florestações. A medida foi transmitida num comunicado enviado às redações. Na mira está o aumento das oportunidades para desenvolvimento de projetos de sequestro de carbono em território nacional e para a captação de investimento privado. Em causa está a geração de um crédito por cada tonelada de CO2 poupada em emissões. Posteriormente, os créditos podem ser vendidos a empresas que queiram libertar carbono para a atmosfera. “Estamos a criar condições para que mais proprietários, entidades e empresas possam investir na floresta e na ação climática", salienta a ministra do Ambiente e da Energia, Maria da Graça Carvalho. O alargamento das metodologias disponíveis permite reforçar "a credibilidade e a capacidade de crescimento do MVC", assim como incentivar ao "financiamento privado para projetos que contribuem simultaneamente para a neutralidade carbónica, valorização do território e resiliência das nossas florestas”, aponta. O MVC conta, à data, com dois projetos registados na metodologia Novas Florestações e um terceiro que aguarda validação inicial. Estão disponíveis para venda 977 créditos de carbono. Para tal, o Portal do Mercado Voluntário de Carbono conta com 29 utilizadores registados, ao mesmo tempo que existem 10 verificadores qualificados para assegurar a validação inicial e a verificação periódica dos projetos, informa o Ministério.

artigo.texto: Democratic incumbent Greg Landsman has proposed legislation that would bar officials from signing nondisclosure agreements when negotiating data center deals — a bill his Republican challenger Eric Conroy says he would support if he wins the seat. WCPO 9 anchor Frank Marzullo spoke one-on-one with both men on data center regulations. Landsman said communities across the country are being shut out of data center negotiations conducted behind closed doors, and that federal guidelines are needed to protect both towns and ratepayers. "We need to protect our towns and our ratepayers. And to say, well, this is a local decision is to say you're on your own, and I don't think that's fair to towns and ratepayers," Landsman said. Landsman pushed back on the argument that federal protections would undercut local authority, saying they would in fact give communities more leverage — including the ability to put data center decisions to a community vote. WATCH: One-on-one with Democratic incumbent Greg Landsman on data centers "Let's have it. If a community wants to go to the ballot. They can do that. Nothing about federal guidelines or federal protections precludes local control. In fact, it just gives them more leverage, and that, I think, is what people want, which is to say, yeah, maybe a data center is OK, but I want to say I don't want the data center to come in. Without me knowing any of the details, buy up a bunch of land, jack up my utility bill, and take all our water. That's they want to be protected," Landsman said. When told his opponent had expressed support for the bill, Landsman reacted positively. "Yes, yes, it's a great bill," Landsman said. Marzullo spoke with Conroy, who told him he would support the legislation if he were in the House. Conroy said data centers are primarily a local matter, but agreed that all negotiations must be conducted openly and in public view. WATCH: One-on-one with Republican challenger Eric Conroy on data centers "First and foremost, I think it's a local issue. So if a local community decides that they want a data center, I'll help them with that. If they decide they don't want a data center, I'll also help them with that. But I think what's very important is that all the debates and discussions are above board and for the public to hear. We need big tech to foot most of the bill, whether that's with utilities or other facilities needed in a community, right? If we lost the battle for the internet 30 years ago as a country, we'd be in a very different spot. So I think we should keep an open mind on data centers, but at the same," Conroy said.

artigo.texto: Google AI data center project investigated after 420 football fields of Finnish forest razed — trees were removed before a mandatory environmental impact assessment, say reports 300 hectares of Finland's forest gobbled up by data center development. Google’s latest data center construction project in Finland is being investigated after the company representing the search giant allegedly cleared over 300 hectares of forest. The reported issue is that Google’s local operator, Tuike Finland, cleared the 420 football fields' worth of trees without obtaining a mandatory environmental impact assessment beforehand, says AFP. Google sees Finland as an attractive European data center host country due to a number of favorable factors. The source notes that it is a country with a cool climate, plus stable and cheap energy supplies (mostly nuclear, wind and hydro). Moreover, Finland sees data centers as a solution to address some current woes such as slow economic growth and record-high unemployment levels. This new development near Muhos, a small town with fewer than 9,000 residents, isn’t the first for Google in Finland. It already has a facility up and running in Hamina, in the south, but hopes to expand in Muhos, Kajaani, and Vaala, in the north. Overall, it is a massive expansion project, and part of a 13-billion-euro ($15-billion) investment in Finland over the next two years. Finland’s potential data center appeal has also made it a location of choice for Microsoft and TikTok. While the local mayor looks forward to the massive investment, growth of business, and general economic boom for the region, residents are waking up to the experience of others where data centers have sprung up. Concerns about impacts on the environment, energy supply stability, and energy prices are simmering under the surface. Google seems to have trampled on some of these concerns already, with these reports of trees already felled and excavators clearing the ground before government agency approval. Not a good start. "In our view, operations at this construction site should be suspended until it is clarified whether the project is in compliance with the law," Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the board of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, told AFP at the edge of the freshly deforested area near Muhos. Even some nature preservation areas have been logged, reckons the chair. Halmeenpaa was responsible for filing the suspension request with the conservation agency. Google denies prematurely devastating the forest. It told AFP that tree felling had been "in compliance with Forestry Act requirements." Moreover, its Finland comms manager said, in a contrasting statement to that of Halmeenpaa, that Google has been ensuring "high-value nature zones within the sites have been protected during forestry works." Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. We haven’t seen any other reports indicating that preparation and construction work has ceased at the new data center development site near Muhos. So it seems like Google will plow ahead, hoping or knowing that the political and/or business will is sufficiently strong to ensure it won’t have to undo any of the actions it has already completed. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

Atualizado
A apuração dos votos para governador de Rondônia no primeiro turno das Eleições 2026 poderá ser acompanhada ao vivo, no site do O GLOBO, neste 4 de outubro. A partir das 17h (horário de Brasília), horário em que termina a votação em todo país, os votos serão atualizados no ambiente especial de apuração do O GLOBO ao mesmo tempo em que são contabilizados e publicados no site do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

CEOs de Anthropic, OpenAI, Google e xAI querem mesmo desacelerar o ritmo da inteligência artificial?
Declarações alarmistas a respeito dos riscos da tecnologia não causam impacto significativo no lançamento de produtos. Idas e vindas do setor refletem também pano de fundo geopolítico e gargalos de infraestrutura
Os principais líderes da inteligência artificial (IA) soaram novamente um estridente alarme sobre os riscos existenciais da tecnologia e concordaram que precisam ajustar o ritmo de desenvolvimento. O tom alarmista não é inédito, o que levanta a questão: será que desta vez eles estão realmente dispostos a cadenciar o ritmo da tecnologia?
O histórico ajuda a aumentar a desconfiança sobre o descolamento entre discurso e ações. Dario Amodei, fundador da Anthropic, se acostumou ao morde e assopra. Quando era líder de segurança da OpenAI, ele se recusou a lançar o GPT-2 devido aos seus riscos — meses depois o modelo estava disponível.
Em maio de 2023, ele assinou um documento que comparava a IA a armas nucleares — um mês depois, o Claude 2 foi lançado. Em 2025, seis dias depois de lançar o Claude 4, ele declarou que a IA elevaria a taxa de desemprego global para 20%.
Agora, especialistas apontam que o setor pode estar, de fato, preocupado com aquilo que está observando em seus testes, especialmente no que diz respeito à capacidade de alguns modelos criar de forma autônoma incidentes cibernéticos — a enxurrada de invasões de sites e plataformas envolvendo Anthropic, Google e, principalmente, OpenAI vem causando um crescente desconforto sobre as práticas de segurança das companhias.
Apesar disso, o ritmo de lançamentos permanece praticamente inalterado. Dez dias após a carta de Amodei que pede nova cadência para o setor, Anthropic e OpenAI lançaram novos modelos, enquanto a SpaceXAI, de Elon Musk, fez o mesmo um dia antes.
Na semana passada, OpenAI e Google afirmaram que deixaram de lançar publicamente novas IAs por questões de segurança — o Google vinha sofrendo críticas por não apresentar modelos de ponta no mesmo ritmo dos rivais, então anunciou o Gemini 4 Argon sem disponibilizá-lo publicamente. É um sinal de que o setor seguirá acelerado.
— O desenvolvimento não vai parar. A questão aqui é o quanto esse discurso é bem-intencionado ou só uma jogada para preservar posicionamento. Existe um contexto geopolítico. A China não vai desacelerar por um motivo simples: por lá, a dominância não é dos empresários. Ela é estatal. E a China tem uma necessidade absurda de dominância. Então, ela está com pé no acelerador — explica Egon Daxbacher, professor do Instituto de Tecnologia e Liderança (Inteli).
Robô assassino made in usa
De fato, a China rejeitou a ideia de desacelerar o desenvolvimento da tecnologia. Em 14 de setembro, Guo Jiakun, do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China, afirmou: "O alarmismo, o confronto e a concorrência desleal só irão atrapalhar o processo de governança global da IA e não servirão aos interesses de ninguém".Frear o dese

‘Capacidade de data centers pode duplicar ou triplicar’ com o Redata, diz CEO da Positivo Tecnologia
O Redata, programa de benefícios tributários para data centers aprovado em setembro no Congresso, pode duplicar ou triplicar a capacidade instalada no país, um boom na demanda por componentes, diz Hélio Bruck Rotenberg, CEO da Positivo Tecnologia.
Nos últimos anos, a fabricante brasileira de computadores se diversificou para oferecer peças, como servidores, e serviços de tecnologia da informação (TI). Hoje, 70% da receita bruta da companhia, cerca de R$ 4 bilhões por ano, vêm do segmento corporativo.
Para Rotenberg, com o Redata e investimentos em inteligência artificial (IA), o Brasil pode se tornar um celeiro de data centers, se aproveitando da corrida tecnológica que opõe EUA e China. A seguir, os principais trechos da entrevista.
Como avalia o Redata?
Somos fornecedores de servidores para data centers, que são o insumo principal deles. O Redata vai dinamizar o mercado de data centers, porque estava todo mundo esperando essa legislação, todo mundo queria pagar menos imposto. Há um pipeline de data centers esperando essa definição.
Definida a lei, faltam algumas regulamentações, evidentemente, e esses investimentos vão acontecer a partir de agora. Como fornecedores de servidores, seremos coabilitados do Redata. Esse é o termo que a lei trouxe. Com essa dinâmica, o mercado aumenta exponencialmente, o que é muito bom.
Estávamos bastante ansiosos em saber se a lei iria proteger a indústria nacional ou se, simplesmente, iria beneficiar a importação de servidores pros data centers, já que, para os operadores, não importa se está beneficiando a empresa nacional ou não, importa que ele compre o servidor mais barato.
A proteção à indústria nacional veio a contento?

Ronaldo Caiado elege sucessor ao governo de Goiás no primeiro turno
Daniel Vilela, de 42 anos, construiu a carreira política sob a influência do pai, Maguito Vilela, e consolidou sua trajetória ao lado do presidenciável do PSD, de quem foi vice-governador
Daniel Vilela, de 42 anos, foi eleito governador de Goiás no primeiro turno neste domingo, dando continuidade ao projeto político iniciado por Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) no estado. Atual governador e candidato à reeleição pelo MDB, Vilela chegou ao Palácio das Esmeraldas depois de uma trajetória marcada pela atuação como vereador, deputado estadual e federal e pela parceria política com Caiado. Vilela recebeu 59,1% dos votos, contra o segundo lugar, Wilder Morais (PL), que ficou com 21,9%.
- Eleições 2026: Veja a apuração ao vivo
Filho do ex-governador e ex-senador Maguito Vilela, Daniel nasceu em Jataí, no Sudoeste goiano, mas cresceu em Goiânia. Antes de entrar para a política, foi jogador de futebol nas categorias de base do Goiás e do Atlético Goianiense. Formou-se em Direito pela Universidade Salgado de Oliveira (Universo) e fez pós-graduação em administração pública pela Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV).
O senador Wilder Morais (PL) terminou em segundo lugar. O petista Luis Cesar Bueno (PT) surpreendeu e ficou à frente do ex-governador Marconi Perillo (PSDB).
Da derrota para Caiado à aliança que o levou ao governo
A carreira política de Vilela começou em 2008, quando foi eleito vereador de Goiânia, aos 24 anos. Dois anos depois, chegou à Assembleia Legislativa e, em 2014, foi eleito deputado federal. Em 2016, assumiu a presidência regional do MDB e, dois anos depois, disputou o governo de Goiás contra Caiado, então adversário político. Foi derrotado no primeiro turno.
A relação entre os dois mudou no ciclo eleitoral seguinte. Em 2022, Vilela foi escolhido como vice na chapa de Caiado, que venceu a reeleição no primeiro turno. A dupla passou a comandar um governo que alcançou altos índices de aprovação no estado. Em 2026, com Caiado lançado à Presidência da República pelo PSD, Vilela assumiu o governo e passou a encabeçar a disputa pela permanência do grupo no Palácio das Esmeraldas.
Na campanha, o governador apresentou como marcas da administração a segurança pública, a expansão da estrutura de saúde e a melhora da situação fiscal de Goiás. Entre os próximos desafios apontados por ele estão os efeitos da reforma tributária, as mudanças climáticas e o fortalecimento das cadeias produtivas diante das tensões comerciais internacionais.
Vilela também defendeu ampliar a produção industrial de Goiás com o uso de inteligência artificial e transformar o estado em um fornecedor relevante de minerais críticos para o mercado internacional.

O Brasil quer data centers ou inteligência?
País precisa investir em infraestrutura para ampliar pesquisa, formação de pesquisadores e desenvolvimento tecnológico
O Brasil deve investir em data centers? A pergunta parece ter uma resposta óbvia.
A inteligência artificial avança rapidamente, grandes modelos exigem quantidades crescentes de processamento e os data centers se tornaram uma das infraestruturas mais disputadas do planeta. Nosso país tem energia, território, água, mercado e posição geográfica privilegiada. Parece uma oportunidade que não podemos perder.
Mas talvez estejamos começando a discussão pelo lado de fora do prédio.
Um data center é uma infraestrutura física. Dentro dele estarão processadores, algoritmos, modelos, dados e, principalmente, conhecimento. É aí que se trava a verdadeira disputa da inteligência artificial.
Construir data centers no Brasil é importante. Mais importante será decidir se seremos só o lugar onde as máquinas estarão instaladas ou se participaremos da ciência e da tecnologia que funcionarão dentro delas.
Estive recentemente em Pequim e Xangai, na China, e voltei com essa impressão muito forte. Na China, o debate sobre inteligência artificial não está apartado da discussão sobre ciência, formação de pessoas, semicondutores, capacidade computacional, energia e desenvolvimento tecnológico.
Diante das restrições ao acesso aos chips mais avançados, por exemplo, a resposta chinesa não foi simplesmente esperar que eles voltassem a estar disponíveis. Buscaram novas arquiteturas, integração de sistemas e outras maneiras de obter capacidade computacional. A escassez obrigou a procurar outro caminho.
Há uma lição importante aí para o Brasil. Podemos atrair bilhões de reais para construir data centers e ainda assim permanecer na periferia tecnológica da inteligência artificial. Ter máquinas funcionando em nosso território não significa necessariamente dominar aquilo que elas fazem.
O ReData avançou ao estabelecer contrapartidas para pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação. A lei determina que empresas beneficiadas invistam no país recursos em projetos de P&D e inovação, inclusive em parceria com instituições científicas, tecnológicas e universidades. É uma direção importante. Mas o tamanho da oportunidade exige pensar além da contrapartida.
Ciência não deveria ser o pedágio pago para construir um data center.
Mais ainda, data centers funcionam dia e noite, faça sol ou não, haja vento ou não. Por que o Brasil, que dispõe de gás em abundância, abriria mão dessa fonte para cargas contínuas e recorreria a enormes sistemas de baterias –tudo importado–? Como já discuti aqui, podemos só trocar uma dependência por outra. Nossa vantagem está justamente na diversificação energética.
E aqui surge outro problema. Estamos planejando grandes infraestruturas para uma tecnologia cuja eficiência muda numa velocidade extraordinária. A Agência Internacional de Energia estima forte crescimento do consumo elétrico dos datacenters nesta década.

TAIPEI, Oct 5 (Reuters) - Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an on Monday defended the city as welcoming and inclusive after a police raid of a gay bar sparked protests by the LGBTQ+ community over alleged discrimination and official misconduct.
One video of the weekend raid that circulated on social media showed a police officer asking a customer in a wheelchair who was in the toilet how disabled people "manage to have sex in there".
Sign up here.
Chiang, who faces reelection next month, said he deeply regretted "improper conduct" by police.
Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage in 2019 in a first for Asia and is normally a bastion of tolerance in a region where LGBTQ+ rights are often suppressed or outlawed. Taipei holds its main Pride event later this month, the largest in East Asia.
Taipei police raided the Commander D bar in the city's main gay neighbourhood of Ximen on Saturday afternoon, citing a complaint alleging the bar could be violating public decency laws. They took 51 people in for questioning and arrested the owner.
Police said on Sunday they had taken disciplinary action against officers for "inappropriate conduct" during the operation, without elaborating.
Chiang, who has previously attended Taipei Pride, said regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, identity, ethnicity or beliefs, the government must ensure everyone in Taipei enjoys equal rights.
"Taipei has always been an inclusive and friendly city for us," he said.
Chiang, of the opposition Kuomintang, is locked in a tight election race against Puma Shen of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party.
Shen said in a Facebook post on Monday that while any illegality should be handled according to the law, people's rights and dignity should be respected.
"Taipei's diversity and inclusivity should not only be visible on Pride parade day," he wrote.
RIGHTS GROUPS ANGERED
The Commander D raid was one of three operations on Saturday involving Ximen gay bars, police precinct spokesperson Chen Yu-cheng told Reuters. Police had in the past conducted "irregular inspections" of the three venues, he said.
Chen added that the precinct inspected 15 entertainment venues on Saturday.
Rights groups say there is a deeper problem.
"This was not a case of individual officers misspeaking or a single instance of excessive enforcement, but the resurfacing of long-standing homophobia, discrimination and abuse of power within the police enforcement system," the Taiwan Alliance to Promote Civil Partnership Rights said in a joint statement with other groups condemning the raid.
One person among the 51 taken in for questioning said they had been detained for more than six hours after police accused them of violating a law that prohibits "wantonly exposing one's naked body or presenting a lascivious posture in a public place."
The person, who requested anonymity, said they had removed their shirt only shortly before police arrived because the bar was crowded and hot.

Wall Street isnât built for consortiums. Blood feuds flourish, and the pressure to outperform rivals leaves little reason to team up with them on investments. But the sheer size of the AI buildout has competitors playing nice.
